The proposed antenna is fabricated by using in-house silicon-based microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) photosensitive composite film fabrication process. The measured gain is 7 dBi at 92 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 81.4 GHz to 109 GHz. The self-packaged antenna shows some advantages and can be further integrated with other components.

articleTitle: An Alternative N-Port Characteristic-Mode Formulation for Lossy Structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a novel N-port characteristic mode (CM) formulation is proposed. By developing the weighting matrix appropriately and solving the proposed generalized eigenvalue equation, the obtained eigenvalues possess significant physical interpretation. Most importantly, the contributions of the radiated, dissipated, and reactive powers can be separated by the obtained eigenvalues. Numerical results of several antennas in lossy environments validate that the proposed N-port CM formulation not only reveals the resonant CMs within the considered frequency band but also further identifies the modal radiation efficiency of each CM.

articleTitle: Wearable Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna with Characteristic Mode Analysis for Wireless Body Area Network Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a flexible, wearable, broadband circularly polarized antenna. A novel polarized conversion metasurface is loaded onto the flexible antenna, greatly expanding impedance and axial ratio bandwidths with the size of 52.6 mm × 49.6 mm × 6.325 mm (0.91 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.86 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.11 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = 5.2 GHz). Besides, Characteristic Mode Analysis is applied to reveal the working mechanism of the antenna. Experimental results indicate that an impedance bandwidth of 4.48-8.39 GHz (60.8%) and a 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 4.43-6.52 GHz (38.2%) could be achieved. Additionally, when the human tissue is 10 g, the peak specific absorption rate (SAR) is 0.3800 W/kg, which is far below the limits of 2.0 W/kg under the 10 g average. The conducted robustness analysis demonstrates the antenna's exceptional stability under various operational conditions, making it a promising candidate for integration into wearable sensor systems.

articleTitle: Near Field Angle Measurement of HPM Helical Array Antennas With its Closed-Loop Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Measuring the pointing angles of high-power microwave (HPM) helical array antennas presents significant challenges, resulting in a lack of effective angle control schemes in current research. To address this issue, this study proposes a near-field pointing detection method that utilizes dipole antennas for closed-loop control of HPM helical array antenna positioning. The evaluation results obtained via interpolation methods show that the absolute angle error is less than 0.701<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^\circ$</tex-math></inline-formula>. In addition, this work also conducted closed-loop control experiments on HPM helical array antennas based on proportional- integral-derivative (PID) control algorithm. Compared to conventional open-loop control systems, the proposed closed-loop control strategy produces a control curve that closely aligns with the theoretical calculation curve, realizing lower steady-state error and improved system robustness.

articleTitle: The Evaporation Duct Characteristics of Typhoon Kompasu (202118) Based on Buoys Observation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Evaporation ducts, which are created due to evaporation from the ocean, significantly affect electromagnetic propagation in coastal and marine areas. Based on air temperature, relative humidity, air pressure, sea surface temperature, and wind speed data from four buoy stations in the northern South China Sea, the evaporation duct height (EDH) characteristics of Typhoon Kompasu (202118) are analyzed using the Naval-Postgraduate-School model. The findings are given as follows: first, the increased mass, momentum, and heat exchanges between the air and sea during a typhoon significantly affect the horizontal homogeneity of temperature and humidity from the ocean surface, especially in the areas where the center of the typhoon passes through. Second, the low-value center of EDH forming at the typhoon center, and typhoon Kompasu increases the nonuniformity of the EDH between the area centered around the typhoon and other regions, with a maximum EDH difference of over 10 m. Third, the main impact factors of EDH between buoy stations at different locations of Typhoon Kompasu are different.

articleTitle: Fast Construction of Measurement Matrix and Sensing Matrix With Dual Adaptive Cross Approximation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: To accelerate the solution of current coefficients in the compressive sensing method of moments, a new strategy for constructing the measurement matrix is proposed, as well as the sensing matrix is optimized. First, the far-field group matrices in the impedance matrix are compressed using the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm, and the row indexes generated during the compression process are used as an extraction strategy rather than random or uniform extraction to construct the measurement matrix. Second, the ACA is used again, which approximates the far-field group matrices in the measurement matrix as the product of two low-rank matrices, resulting in a part-constructed sensing matrix. The dual ACA not only maintains computational accuracy, but also saves memory consumption, improving computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Topology Optimization Method for Designing Modularized Subarrayed Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Modularized subarrayed phased arrays are presented in this work to reduce design complexity and improve circular polarization performance. To minimize the loss of the beam scanning performance caused by modularization, a hierarchical topology optimization method is presented. It optimizes module orientations and the common subarray layout in the modules by a two-level optimization process, ensuring that the loss of the beam scanning performance is not significant. As a result, the designed array can still maintain relatively good beam scanning performance on the premise of low design complexity, high boresight directivity and good circular polarization performance. A series of comparison results are provided.

articleTitle: An Energy-Perturbation-Based Configuration Strategy for Multifunctional Microstrip Antennas Design
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A new configuration strategy for multifunctional microstrip antennas design based on energy flow manipulation is proposed in this paper. The proposed method utilizes the Poynting streamline technique to visualize the effective aperture of the antenna and the energy flow characteristics, offering a novel and intuitive auxiliary approach to antenna design from the perspective of energy modulation. The configuration strategies for antenna gain enhancement and beamwidth expansion through energy perturbation are discussed in detail in this letter. This method can also be extended to the design of multifunctional reconfigurable antennas. The method is demonstrated using both linearly polarized and dual-polarized planar antennas. The results show that the proposed strategy enables the design of antenna configurations that meet specific performance requirements, while also offering insights into the physical mechanisms that allow the design to achieve its performance targets.

articleTitle: Design of Artificial Metal Rough Surfaces for Ultrawideband RCS Reduction Based on Approximate Ray Launching Geometrical Optics
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes an approximate ray launching geometrical optics (ARL-GO) method for designing the profiles of 1-D and 2-D artificial metal rough surfaces (AMRSs) to realize ultrawideband radar cross section (RCS) reduction. The method transforms AMRS's height and gradient into the electromagnetic wave's amplitude and phase, achieving fast calculation of AMRS's RCS. Combined with the constrained multiobjective particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, the AMRSs can format good diffuse scattering of incoming plane waves. Under normal incidence, the final optimized polarization-insensitive 1-D and 2-D AMRSs can realize 20 dB RCS reduction at frequencies of above 7.6 GHz and 6.7 GHz, respectively, with no upper limit frequency. While the incident angle reaches 40°, the designed AMRSs can still achieve 20 dB RCS reduction above 10 GHz, achieving good stealth performance. The theoretical analysis, simulation, and experimental results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave High-Gain Shorted Patch Antenna Using Hybrid TM2,1/2 and TM3,1/2 Modes
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Using a higher-order patch radiator is an effective approach to realizing a high-gain antenna. This paper proposes a method of designing a high-gain millimeter-wave shorted patch antenna by exciting hybrid TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1/2</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3,1/2</sub> modes. Higher-order shorted patch has half size of the conventional patch, but its radiation pattern is split into dual beams with reduced gain in TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1/2</sub> mode. To tackle this problem, slots are etched on the shorted patch edge to adjust the current distribution, generating additional magnetic current. As a result, the proposed shorted patch antenna has reshaped standard broadside radiation pattern at two resonance frequencies of 24 and 29 GHz, corresponding to TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1/2</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3,1/2</sub> modes, respectively. Therefore, the antenna operating bandwidth is enhanced to be 23.3-30.3 GHz, and the in-band gain is up to 10.6 dBi. Sawtooth-shaped stubs are used for further miniaturization. Compared with previously reported patch antennas, the proposed antenna has more compact size, higher gain and wider bandwidth.

articleTitle: Dual-Broadband Vertically Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna with Low Profile
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A dual-broadband vertically polarized omnidirec-tional patch antenna with simple low-profile structure is proposed for mobile communication. The design is formed by a wheel-shaped patch, a circular ground reflector, four arc-shaped strips, four feeding pins, eight shorting pins and a 1-to-4 power divider. The wheel-shaped patch, connected to the ground reflector by eight shoring pins, is fed by the 1-to-4 power divider to generate four TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> or TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> resonant modes. Then four arc-shaped strips are embedded in the wheel-shaped patch to generate an extra TM01 resonant mode. Based on the new scheme, five resonant modes are inspired to form two wide frequency bands. The proposed antenna exhibits dual broad bandwidths of 38.6% (1.63-2.41 GHz) and 47.4% (3.17-5.14 GHz). Additionally, the proposed design has a simply two-layer structure and a thin profile of 0.058λL, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> represents the free-space wavelength at the lowest operating band, which makes it suitable for indoor mobile communication systems within the bands of GSM1800/IMT2000/ LTE2300 and 5G NR 78/79.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Independent Wideband Switchable Rasorber With High Roll-Off Characteristics Utilizing Third-Order Switchable FSS
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In recent years, switchable frequency selective rasorbers (FSRs) have been extensively studied due to their in-band shielding ability. However, it is difficult to achieve dual-polarized switchable FSR with wide passband and excellent roll-off characteristics simultaneously. In this letter, a polarization-independent wideband switchable FSR with high roll-off characteristics is proposed. The FSR is composed of a three-layer architecture with a nonswitchable impedance layer, a switchable impedance layer and a switchable frequency selective surface (FSS). A switchable FSS with third-order response is utilized to achieve low profile, wideband transmission and high roll-off characteristics. Meanwhile, a wide low reflection band is achieved with the assistance of two impedance layers. Under each polarization, the device can be independently switched between rasorber and absorber modes. Finally, a prototype is manufactured and measured to demonstrate the viability of the proposed design. Compared with the existing counterparts, the proposed dual-polarized switchable FSR exhibits excellent performance in terms of wideband transmission, high roll-off characteristics and broadband absorption.

articleTitle: A Flexible Multifunctional Absorber/Reflector with Wideband and Low Power Performance
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper presents a multifunctional flexible absorber/reflector with wideband performance and low power consumption. The proposed unit cell utilizes only two PIN diodes to achieve four distinct functions with low power consumption. By integrating the metal structure of the unit cell with the PIN diode bias lines, the design is simplified. In addition, the physical characteristics of the proposed structure are thoroughly analyzed using equivalent circuit theory, electric field analysis, and surface current distribution, enhancing the understanding of the design mechanisms. The simulation and experimental verification results are in agreement. Four distinct functions are successfully demonstrated within the frequency band of 8.5 GHz - 12.5 GHz, with a maximum power consumption of only 0.078 W.

articleTitle: Theory of an Arbitrarily Oriented Multi-Feed Linear Antenna in a Cold Magnetoplasma
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, an analytical method for studying the theory of an arbitrarily oriented multi-feed very-low-frequency (VLF: 3-30 kHz) linear antenna in a cold magnetoplasma is proposed. The node currents and admittances are calculated by solving the matrix equation. Analysis and computations show that the current concentrates on multiple feed points and amplitudes will decrease when the dip angle rises. It is also found that both the self- and mutual admittances will decrease in general with the increase of the dip angle and the electrical length, respectively. The approach can provide theoretical assistance and technical guidance for practical space-borne multi-feed antennas in the near future.

articleTitle: Phased Array Antenna with Reduced Phase Shifters Using a Passive Overlapped Mapping Feeding Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel phased array antenna (PAA) design employing a passive overlapped mapping feeding network (POMFN) to reduce the number of phase shifters while enhancing gain and suppressing grating lobes. By leveraging a multiple-center feeding structure with cascaded transmission lines, the POMFN maps phase-shifted ports to multiple radiating elements, increasing array aperture size and achieving aperture overlap. This results in a near-sinc function aperture field, producing a flat-top active unit cell pattern that suppresses grating lobes and reduces scan loss during beam scanning. Two 10-GHz planar PAA prototypes with λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and 1.5λ0 phase-shifted port spacings are designed. The first has five phase-shifted ports spaced by λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> feeding 4×16 elements, demonstrating a 22.5-dBi peak gain, a scanning range up to ±18° with 2.3-dB gain variation, and a -11.8-dB sidelobe level (SLL). The second prototype has five phase-shifted ports spaced by 1.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> feeding 4×21 elements, exhibiting a 24.1-dBi peak gain, a scanning range of ±12° with 1.3-dB gain variation, and an SLL below -10.9 dB. Compared with its former counterparts, this design offers a cost-effective and simplified structural solution for limited field of view applications requiring high performance and low grating lobes.

articleTitle: A 1-bit Reconfigurable Antenna Array with Radiation and Scattering Modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This work proposes an electrically tunable reconfigurable antenna array with wideband radiation and scattering modulation using a simpler structure and an easier control mechanism. A ladder-shaped patch is designed as the radiator. By inserting only one PIN diode in the middle of the patch structure, its operation can be modulated between a patch mode and a slot mode, achieving a wideband reflection phase difference of 180°±37°. A 4 × 4 array is formed using the aforementioned element, which can reconfigure its radiation and scattering modes by controlling the states of the PIN diodes. The measured results show that the proposed array exhibits a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 20.99% with a peak gain of 14.94 dBi in the radiation mode. In the scattering mode, the phase distributions of the elements are optimized by Group Search Optimizer (GSO) algorithm. The radar cross section (RCS) is reduced in the frequency range of 6 - 20 GHz with an average RCS reduction value of 17 dB in the operating band.

articleTitle: Design of Large-Span Beamforming Antenna Based on Beam Superposition and Structure Mapping
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this paper, a novel beamforming patch array antenna with large-span cosecant-distribution pattern is designed. The antenna contains two layers, and eight radiating patch elements together with feeding microstrip branches are designed on the upper surface of the top layer. The bottom layer is a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) with a series of slots cut in the upper wall, which couple the energy in SIW up to the feeding microstrip branches. Five linear arrays are designed first to generate beams with different radiation angles, and then mapped into a composite array in a weighted way to generate a large-span cosecant-distribution pattern, and minimize the size of antenna. The proposed antenna can provide a uniform radio wave coverage in long-straight confined spaces for stable mobile communications.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS Analysis of Finite Periodic Array in the Vicinity of Object Using Modified SSED-CBFM and Improved FIR
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: We propose an accurate and efficient method for the wideband analysis of a finite periodic array near an object. It elegantly combines the merits of the modified simplified subentire domain (SSED)-characteristic basis function method (CBFM) and the improved frequency-independent reaction (FIR). It constructs the SSED basis functions on the array cell and CBFs on the object and, thus, obtains the SSED-CBFs-based reduced matrix equation. The improved FIR accelerates the computation of the impedance matrices at each frequency. Our new method keeps high accuracy in the numerical examples while greatly reducing the total CPU time.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain Quad-Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna Using Three-Layered Polarizer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Quad-polarization reconfigurable antenna consists of a three-layered polarizer and an 8 × 8 source antenna is investigated in the Ka-band. By changing the orientation of each layer, the antenna can radiate horizontally polarized, vertically polarized, left-hand and right-hand circularly polarized electromagnetic waves. The 8 × 8 horn array is employed as the source antenna, enhancing the antenna gain and expanding the operating bandwidth. The polarizer and the source antenna are fabricated by 3-D printing technology using photopolymer and aluminum alloy. Excellent operating performance including impedance bandwidth of 51.1%, gain up to 24.8 dBi, dual circular polarization overlap bandwidth of 41.3%, and quad-polarization overlap bandwidth of 24.6% is obtained experimentally by fabricated prototype. The proposed antenna with promising performance is valuable to emerging millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: A Wide-Angle and Ultrawideband Van Atta Array for Monostatic RCS Enhancement
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The limited applications of current Van Atta arrays in various fields are primarily due to their narrow working bandwidths. This letter designed an ultrawideband Van Atta retrodirective array. It is based on the generalized phase conjugation principle and leverages the wideband characteristics of the Vivaldi antenna. This array exhibits excellent retrodirective performance over the frequency range of 2.42 GHz to 29.71 GHz, boasting a relative working bandwidth of 170%. To verify the design, a prototype was fabricated and its retrodirective performance was measured over the 2.42 GHz to 18.2 GHz frequency range. The measured results correlate well with the simulated ones. Specifically, the beamwidth remains within ±30°, and the variation in the monostatic radar cross section (RCS) value of the array does not surpass 3 dB. Compared to a metal plate of equal area, the monostatic RCS exhibits an enhancement of 10 dB to 20 dB. This design, with a wide bandwidth and wide-angle retrodirection capabilities, is poised to significantly impact the research and application of Van Atta arrays.

articleTitle: A Wideband Millimeter-Wave Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna With a Stacked Strip Using SISL Technology for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A wideband millimeter-wave circularly polarized (CP) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed in this letter based on substrate-integrated suspended line (SISL). To generate CP waves, a square DRA is cut off two corners. The introduction of the dielectric ring not only serves to fix the DR, but also improves the antenna matching and axial ratio bandwidth. In order to increase the axial ratio bandwidth and realized gain, a stacked strip is introduced on the C1 layer. The proposed antenna is fabricated and measured, and the measured results show the antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 27.94%, which is from 23.4 GHz to 31 GHz. The axial ratio bandwidth of 30.55% is from 23.3 GHz to 31.7 GHz, and the measured peak gain is 7.5 dBic.

articleTitle: A Pattern-Reconfigurable, Compact, Wideband Filtering Directive Dipole Antenna Enabled With Mixed Couplings
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A pattern-reconfigurable, compact, wideband filtering directive dipole antenna enabled with mixed couplings is presented. Due to the mixed couplings in a single-fed multiple-element dipole antenna, the generated phase differences between resonators contribute to the filtering response and directive radiating performance simultaneously within a close element spacing. Based on this design methodology, two switchable opposite directive endfire states can be accomplished by controlling the ON/OFF operating states of the four PIN diodes integrated into a pair of custom-designed parasitic elements. A prototype operating at about 1.2 GHz is designed, fabricated, and measured. The measured results, in good agreement with simulated results, demonstrate that the antenna exhibits 22.4% wide operational bandwidth and 4.5 dBi realized gain values at a compact size of 0.21λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.33λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. A good out-of-band rejection level of 12 dB is also achieved in both states. The proposed antenna can be employed in space-limited communication systems, e.g., vehicle-to-vehicle scenarios and indoor wireless network systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Grating Lobe Suppression Method for Large-Spacing Phased Arrays Using Prephased Metalens and Limited Random Phase
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The electronically steered phased array (ESPA), which is composed of periodic antenna elements, usually uses subarrays with large spacing to lower system complexity and cost. This kind of phased subarray (PSA) has a serious problem with grating lobes while beam scanning. A prephased metalens PSA (PMPSA) that combines prephases and metalens for modifying the transmitting phases is proposed. Further, the limited random phase method (LRPM) for randomizing the feeding phases and cooperating with prephased metalens to suppress the grating lobes is also proposed. In comparison to a PSA with the same parameters, the results demonstrate that the PMPSA can achieve a much better SLL, especially at wide scanning angles. Finally, calculated and simulated results show that a 16 × 16-unit phased array with 2 × 2-unit subarrays can achieve an SLL below −9.9 dB in 2D scanning using the limited random phase method.

articleTitle: A Switchable UHF RFID Reader Antenna for Near-Field and Far-Field Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we present a switchable near-field (NF) and far-field (FF) antenna designed for ultrahigh-frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification applications. The antenna consists of a four-dipole array and a feeding network. By adjusting the current distribution through the multiport feeding network, the antenna can either create a strong, uniform magnetic field in the NF region with low FF gain or produce circularly polarized radiation in the FF region. Through the use of segmented lines and parasitic elements, the antenna achieves a flat magnetic field distribution over a large area. The NF and FF modes can operate independently or in polling. A prototype was fabricated and tested, showing that the antenna generates a strong, uniform magnetic field over an interrogation zone of 270 mm × 270 mm in NF mode, while delivering a 3.7 dBic gain in FF mode. These results confirm the antenna's excellent performance in both NF and FF regions, with an isolation of over <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-$</tex-math></inline-formula>22 dB between the two modes.

articleTitle: A Sub-Terahertz Broadband Metasurface-Inspired on-Chip Stacked Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a metasurface-inspired stacked patch on-chip antenna is proposed in a sub-terahertz band. To enhance the bandwidth and gain, the original on-chip patch is evolved to be stacked with metasurface-inspired patches. Characteristic mode analysis verifies that four adjacent resonance modes are introduced by the proposed structure and excited for achieving a wideband operation with excellent radiation performance. For experimental demonstration, a passive on-chip patch is taped out using the back-end-of-line of a SiGe BiCMOS process and assembled with the superstrate antenna. An impedance bandwidth of 33.6% (200-281 GHz) is measured and a maximum gain of 3.4 dBi is achieved at 273 GHz with a maximum radiation efficiency of 51.8%. The proposed hybrid on-chip antenna features broadband impedance matching and a high antenna efficiency, which makes it a promising candidate for 6G communication systems.

articleTitle: Compact High-Efficiency All-Polarization Rectenna for Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we present an innovative design for a compact, high-efficiency all-polarization receiving rectenna tailored for wireless power transmission. This rectenna, which integrates an antenna with two same rectifier units, employs direct conjugate matching of antenna impedance to rectifier impedance. This approach eliminates the necessity for an external impedance-matching network, thereby reducing the overall dimensions of the rectenna. The implementation of virtual ground concept streamlines the design of the rectifier's output filter. The low-profile antenna, engineered for operation at 2.45 GHz, demonstrates high conversion efficiency across all polarization angles. The measured RF-to-DC efficiency exceeds 63% for all polarization angles, achieving a peak efficiency of 82.2%.

articleTitle: A Time–Frequency Domain Adaptive Impedance Matching Approach Based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Frequent fluctuations of antenna impedance within the time–frequency domain of mobile devices require efficient and accurate impedance matching. In this work, we propose an adaptive impedance matching approach based on deep neural network (DNN). Using frequency, voltage standing wave ratio and peak voltages as inputs, this approach employs a DNN to directly output the matching parameters. Compared to traditional analytical methods, the proposed approach reduces the complexity of the detection circuit. That is because the proposed approach requires only the amplitude information of the radio frequency signal to correct mismatches. For a simulated planar inverted-F antenna, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DNN-based approach achieves more efficient iteration-free matching compared to simulated annealing particle swarm optimization and genetic algorithms.

articleTitle: Diagonally Shielded HMSIW-Based Self-Triplexing Radiating Element for 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A compact self-triplexing antenna (STA) operating simultaneously at 5.25 GHz, 28.85 GHz, and 31.9 GHz with better than 33 dB isolation among the frequency bands is presented in this letter. The design is based on a diagonally shielded half-mode substrate integrated waveguide cavity, which is designed by placing an open rectangular slot along the diagonal perfect magnetic wall and a row of metallized vias in a square cavity to shield the RF leakage. The cavity is loaded with two orthogonal modified rectangular slots on its top surface to facilitate triplexing operation. The STA features input reflection better than −10 dB over a fractional bandwidth of 3.79%, 4.16%, and 3.29% at 5.25 GHz, 28.85 GHz, and 31.9 GHz, respectively. The proposed STA has a peak gain of 5.1 dBi, 8.1 dBi, and 8.3 dBi with good cross-polarization levels at 5.25 GHz, 28.85 GHz, and 31.9 GHz, respectively. The STA achieves an efficiency better than 80% and 90% in microwave and mm-wave frequency regimes, respectively. The proposed STA is modeled and fabricated, and simulated results are experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Inspired Circularly Polarized MIMO Antenna for 5G mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter offers metasurface-inspired multiple-input--multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with circular polarization (CP). The antenna radiating element consists of 1 × 2 array nonbianisotropic split ring resonator with an interdigital capacitance. Furthermore, a four-port MIMO antenna is designed with a 8 × 8 metasurface array (M-Array) on the ground plane. The dimensions of the proposed CP MIMO antenna are 4.6<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula><inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\, \times\, \text{4.6}\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula><inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\,\times\, \text{0.128}\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula> at 28 GHz. The MIMO antenna with an M-Array offers a frequency range of 30.15% [(23.8 to 32.25) GHz], isolation above 55 dB and an overlapping 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 14% from 26.5 GHz to 30.5 GHz with a high gain of 18.5 dBi. The proposed MIMO antenna is simplified into an equivalent circuit model. Diversity metrics ensures good diversity performance including, envelope correlation coefficient (ECC <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$< $</tex-math></inline-formula> 0.01), diversity gain (DG <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx$</tex-math></inline-formula> 10 dB), channel capacity loss (CCL <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$< $</tex-math></inline-formula> 0.1 bits/Hz), and total active reflection coefficient (TARC <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$< $</tex-math></inline-formula> –10 dB). The proposed MIMO antenna's operational range includes the mmWave band [(25 to 29.5) GHz]. It is well suited for 5G new radio smart devices due to its better performance and compatibility with 5G communication standards.

articleTitle: Directivity and Image Principle from Reflective Surfaces
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The theory of one or more radiating sources above a reflective surface with an arbitrary reflection coefficient is presented in this letter. Using this generalized approach, it is demonstrated that optimal configurations exist between the sources and the reflective surface. Examples are given for one or two infinitely small electric dipoles above a reflective surface. A maximum directivity of approximately <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$10.2 \ dBi$</tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$14.1 \ dBi$</tex-math></inline-formula> is obtained, respectively. Furthermore, using a more hypothetical approach that considers the reflective behavior of a given surface, a directivity limit for vanishingly small Huygens sources over a generalized reflective surface is derived to be <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ 12 \ dBi$</tex-math></inline-formula>.

articleTitle: Development of Cast Iron Manhole Cover With Broadband-Radio-Transmission Characteristics Applying Spiral Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter reports on a cast iron manhole cover with a slit structure to improve the efficiency of radio propagation from underground structures. The spiral slit of a broadband antenna was applied to the iron cover to achieve broadband radio propagation characteristics. A full-scale manhole model was fabricated and evaluated, resulting in a maximum gain of 2.5 dB and a bandwidth of 193 MHz [(807 to 1000) MHz]. The results of field tests with the prototype showed an average of −77.9 dBm for the slit iron cover and −100.5 dBm for the conventional product in wireless communication from inside a manhole through the iron cover. The 22.6 dBm improvement in radio transmission while maintaining the functionality of the steel cover is sufficiently practical. This result can contribute to the maintenance and management of aging infrastructure and the spread of disaster prevention systems as a technology to reduce the cost of introducing Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems to underground infrastructure.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Transparent Dipole Antenna Based on Frequency Selective Surface and Its Applications in Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Array
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A lower-band (LB) dual-polarized dipole antenna with wideband high-transparent characteristics based on frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed. In order to achieve flexible expansion of transparent bands, four U-shaped stubs are symmetrically loaded on the square ring-shaped arm of LB dipole. Thus, the LB arms can be perceived as the band-pass FSS structure at a higher band (HB) with not only one transmission pole but also two transmission zeros, for which the transparent band can be flexibly regulated and finally a wide passband of 1.7 GHz to 2.75 GHz with high transmission coefficient of over −0.5 dB is easily generated by just one-layer structure. Subsequently, the newly designed LB dipole operating at 0.69 GHz to 0.96 GHz (32.7%) is used to construct a dual-band shared-aperture array, where 2 × 2 HB antennas operating at 1.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz (45.5%) are located beneath it. The simulated results agree well with the measured ones, and the performances of LB and HB antennas in the array are consistent with those working alone, indicating the slight mutual interference between the two antennas, which significantly guarantees the dual-band radiation under the same aperture.

articleTitle: A Wideband and Low-Profile Circularly Polarized Filtering Stacked Back-Cavity Antenna Using Magnetodielectric Materials
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) filtering stacked back-cavity antenna with wideband and low-profile characteristics using magnetodielectric materials is presented in this letter. The proposed antenna consists of a top metal plate, a middle layer with a dual square loop slotted patch, a bottom layer ground plate, a Wilkinson power divider, a metal cavity, and magnetodielectric materials. The aforementioned structures are embedded in a metal cavity that can form a conformal antenna with the communication systems. Most importantly, magnetodielectric materials are utilized to improve impedance bandwidth matching and realize the low-profile characteristic. In addition, the dual square loop slots are etched on the patch, which can generate two radiation nulls and obtain the filtering performance without adding an external filter. Furthermore, the Wilkinson power divider is used to achieve the CP radiation characteristic and operate an excellent axial ratio bandwidth. For verification, a prototype is fabricated and tested with the dimensions of 0.30λ0 × 0.30λ0 × 0.08λ0, where λ0 is the free-space wavelength at the lowest frequency of operation. The simulated and measured results match well that an impedance bandwidth of 37.6% (0.80-1.17 GHz), an axial ratio bandwidth of 34.2% (0.80-1.13 GHz), and a realized gain of 3.25 dBi are achieved. The stopbands have a good out-of-band suppression level of more than 22 dB.

articleTitle: A Scalable Filtering MIMO Antenna with Space Diversity Based on Shared SIW Cavities
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A scalable filtering multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna based on shared substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed in this letter. By fully utilizing the orthogonality of TE130 and TE310 modes, the dual-mode is excited by different feeding ports and transmit in the proposed shared structure but along two directions independently. Only by offsetting feeding points and coupling irises, the isolations between different feeding ports are guaranteed. Half-mode SIWs are cascaded as the last stage radiators. Then, two filtering independent beams are obtained to achieve the space diversity characteristic. Because of the orthogonal modes, the two filtering beams of the two directions can also be scaled to work in different bandwidths, different working frequencies and patterns. The demonstrated filtering MIMO antenna has -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 9.94 to 10.09 GHz, and the isolations are better than 20 dB. More importantly, the utilized filtering resonator number is reduced by half compared with the conventional filter and antenna cascade design.

articleTitle: A Tri-Frequency Shared-Aperture Antenna for Cooperative Work of V2X and Millimeter-Wave Bands
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The microwave (MW)/millimeter-wave (MMW) shared aperture technique is a promising approach to support different frequency bands within limited space. In this letter, a 1 × 4 beam-scanning linear antenna array operating at the MMW (28/39 GHz) band and a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) (5.9 GHz) patch antenna are integrated to share the same aperture. Not only are the entire MMW bands covered, but also the mutually enhanced characteristic between the MW and MMW bands is achieved with the slot-loaded patch. The MW patch nested outside of the MMW radiators can enhance the gain and extend the beam-scanning angles of the MMW antenna array. Furthermore, the hollowed space reserved for MMW antenna can improve the radiation pattern of the MW patch TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> mode. The proposed tri-band antenna was fabricated and measured. Measured results show that the MMW antenna can cover the bandwidths of 24.4 GHz to 29.3 GHz/36.7 GHz to 41.4 GHz, with the peak gains of 11 dBi/11.3 dBi at 28 GHz/39 GHz frequency bands, while the proposed MW antenna achieves a bandwidth of ∼170 MHz with a peak gain of 8.03 dBi.

articleTitle: Reduced Order Modeling for Parameterized Electromagnetic Simulation Based on Free-Form Deformation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: We propose a parametric geometry-based non-intrusive model order reduction (NIMOR) model for electromagnetic simulation in domains of different shapes. The free-from-deformation (FFD) method is introduced to adjust the mesh when the shape changes. This NIMOR model generates a set of reduced-order basis (RB) functions by applying a two-step randomized singular value decomposition (SVD) method with an auto-rank generator (ARRSVD) to the matrix composed of the full-order solutions. A map between the time/geometry parameters and the projection coefficients is approximated by the cubic-spline interpolation (CSI) approach. This reduced-order model (ROM) is trained in the offline stage, while the RB solutions for new parameters can be quickly recovered in the online stage. Numerical experiments show that the proposed NIMOR method can achieve near real-time electromagnetic scattering simulation on domains of different shapes while guaranteeing the accuracy.

Author Keywords: Randomized singular value decomposition method with an auto-rank generator

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Dual-Polarized Array Antenna Using Low-Loss Transmission Line at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A Ka-band high-efficiency 8 × 8 dual-polarized patch array antenna is presented. With air as primary transmission medium, the double-sided even-mode air suspended line (ASL) has low attenuation constant, thereby realizing low-loss transmission. A 2 × 4 sub-array fed by this low-loss line through coupling slots is proposed at 35 GHz. By extending the sub-array, an 8 × 8 dual-polarized array is finally designed. Two independent feeding networks composed of this low-loss transmission line are skillfully designed to excite two orthogonal linear polarizations. The experimental results indicate that the realized maximal gains and the corresponding radiation efficiencies are 22.54 dBi and 74.53% for x-polarization, 23.35 dBi and 87.1% for y-polarization.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Broadband Phase-switched Screen
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The traditional phase-switched screens (PSS) are typically a quarter-wavelength thick and have relatively narrow frequency bands, unfavorable for practical engineering applications. In this paper, we propose a novel PSS designs that changes the states of four PIN diodes to modulate the reflected phase of the PSS between two states (ON and OFF), with a phase difference of 180°±37° across 6.7 to 14.2 GHz range and a corresponding relative bandwidth of 72%. Using digital modulation techniques, the incident wave is efficiently reflected, and its energy is transferred out of the operating band of the radar receiver by digital modulation techniques. Simulation and measurement results validate the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Fourier Neural Operator Enhanced Physics-Embedded Iterative Learning Solver for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, an efficient and accurate physics-embedded Fletcher-Reeves Conjugate Gradient (FRCG) projection method, termed CGFNO, is proposed to solve the electromagnetic scattering problems iteratively. As a neural network, the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) in the proposed method is deployed to facilitate the update of the unknown total electric field directly. In addition, the weight-sharing mechanism inherent in FNO substantially reduces the neural network complexity. The proposed CGFNO, which incorporates neural networks, demonstrates superior performance over the traditional FRCG method, offering improved accuracy and efficiency while significantly reducing both iteration counts and computational time in scattering field calculations. The accuracy and generalization ability of the CGFNO are verified with two representative numerical tests. Comparative analyses further reveal that CGFNO exhibits enhanced computational efficiency compared to the conventional numerical methods.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Broadband Metamaterial Absorber with Angle-insensitive Characteristics Covering the L, S, C, X, and Ku Bands
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents an ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber with angle-insensitive characteristics covering the L, S, C, X, and Ku bands. The proposed metamaterial absorber achieves wave-absorbing properties through the applications of a cross-shaped substrate printed with high-resistance carbon paste and a frequency-dispersive magnetic material (FDMM). Under the combined effect of the two substructure, the absorber realizes an ultra-wide absorption band from 0.84 GHz to 20 GHz with at least -10 dB reflectivity. In addition, the proposed composite metamaterial absorber shows a wide-angle absorbing performance for both TE and TM polarized waves, and the angular stability is up to 60° for TM polarization. With the application of the FDMM, the thickness of the metamaterial absorber is limited to 26.5 mm (0.074). A prototype is fabricated and measured, and the measurement results agreed well with the simulation.

articleTitle: Low-Profile MIMO Trapezoidal Patch Antenna for 5G Wideband Mobile Antenna Application
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a low-profile trapezoidal patch quad antenna for 5G broadband mobile applications. The multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) four-antenna is printed on an FR4 glass fiber substrate with a size of 42 mm × 42 mm (about 0.581λ × 0.581λ at 4.15 GHz) and a thickness of 0.4 mm. The system ground plane is 42 mm × 42 mm, and the air layer is 1.6 mm above the ground plane. The total cross-sectional height is only 2.0 mm (about 0.027λ at 4.15 GHz). The antenna features four identically sized coupled feed structures, each with a 90° rotated trapezoidal patch antenna. A shorting pin near the feeding point is added to improve matching and isolation, successfully covering the sub-6-GHz broadband spectrum from 3.3 GHz to 5.0 GHz and achieving a 41% bandwidth at 4.15 GHz. The isolation between antennas is more than 10 dB. The calculated envelope correlation coefficient values are less than 0.13. The radiation efficiency of the four antennas has been measured to exceed 40%.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Checkerboard Metasurface Based on Reconfigurable Polarization Converter for Dual-Mode RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a reconfigurable broadband multifunctional polarization conversion metasurface (RBMPCM) based on positive-intrinsic-negative (PIN) diode is proposed. The unit of RBMPCM can effectively reflect an x-polarized electromagnetic (EM) waves into its orthogonal polarization as well as circular polarization in a broad frequency band of 8.78 to 14.33 GHz, by changing the state of PIN-diode. A modified ground plane is created to supply a bias voltage to the PIN-diode, hence eliminating the need for additional feeding lines, which could adversely affect the performance of a structure by influencing signal efficiency, radiation pattern, frequency response and overall stability. Next, the polarization converter and its mirror are placed in a standard checkerboard pattern to achieve dual-mode radar cross section (RCS) reduction. Two different samples (periodic and checkerboard) were fabricated and experiments were performed, which showed excellent agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Planar Endfire Antenna With Enhanced Front-to-Back Ratio
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A dual-band endfire antenna with planar structure and high front-to-back ratio (FTBR) is investigated. The antenna is mainly composed of three pairs of dipoles. Connected by parallel double-side compensate lines, a three-dipole array can inform a dual-band operating mode. Moreover, a parasitic strip and a two-stage director are incorporated into the antenna structure to regulate the current distributions of the three dipoles, significantly widening the 15 dB FTBR bandwidth of lower and upper bands. Consequently, the antenna obtains measured overlapping bandwidths (<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|{S}_{\text 11}|$</tex-math></inline-formula> <−10 dB and FTBR >15 dB) of 9.5% [(3.2 to 3.52) GHz] and 35.6% [(4.13 to 5.92) GHz] of the two bands, respectively. The peak gains of the antenna are 7.42 dBi at 3.3 GHz and 9.08 dBi at 5.85 GHz. The proposed methodology of this design can apply to applications related to Wi-MAX/Wi-LAN wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Filtering Transmitarray Antenna Based on 1-Bit Magnetoelectric Dipole
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A filtering transmitarray antenna (TA) based on a filtering antenna to filtering antenna (FA-FA) structure is proposed. The TA unit consists of two identical magnetoelectric (ME) dipoles arranged in a back-to-back configuration, connecting by a metallic via. A stable 1-bit phase adjustment is achieved by physically rotating the receiving or radiating element 180° around the feed point. For experimental validation, a TA prototype incorporating 24×24 of the proposed elements was designed, fabricated, and measured. It demonstrates a 3-dB gain bandwidth ranging from 11.58 to 12.6 GHz (8.4%) and exhibits a gain-filtering response with an out-of-band suppression level of at least 17 dB. With a 10-dB to 3-dB gain bandwidth ratio of 1.16, the antenna demonstrates high-frequency selectivity. The gain remains stable across the operating frequency band of 11.5 to 12.75 GHz. Additionally, the antenna achieves a maximum radiation gain of 22.2 dBi overall frequency, with an aperture efficiency of 20.8%. These characteristics indicate that the proposed design can reduce the need for additional filter circuitry, offering a promising solution to improve the electromagnetic compatibility of communication systems.

articleTitle: Single-Feed Near-Field Excited Quad-Beam Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we propose the design of a single-feed low-profile digitally coded metasurface antenna for generation of quad-beam radiation. The design procedure involves initial synthesis of the desired reflection phase profile using far-field plane-wave illumination, followed by application of a correction factor which considers presence of near-field excitation source generating spherical waves. The profile of the proposed quad-beam metasurface antenna is significantly minimized using a coax-fed printed dipole as exciter, instead of the high-gain helical or horn antennas placed at a distance for feeding conventional reflectarrays. Furthermore, use of 1-bit coding scheme considerably reduces the design complexity of the metasurface. Full-wave EM simulations based on CST Microwave Studio (CST-MWS) and experimental measurements on fabricated prototype confirm that the dipole-excited metasurface with aperture size <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$11\lambda _{0} \times 11\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula> (where <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula> is the free-space wavelength at 10 GHz) generates four symmetrical beams in the <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\theta =45^{\circ}$</tex-math></inline-formula> plane with peak gain of 11.7 dBi. The proposed low-profile quad-beam metasurface antenna has potential to be used in future 6G communications as well as X-band radar applications.

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of Highly Resonant Transmitarray Element For Sub-THz 6G Communications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An efficient analysis technique for a transmitarray (TA) unit cell based on a method of moments (MoM) in the spectral domain assuming local periodicity is proposed. The MoM employs basis functions consisting of Chebyshev polynomials weighed by a function that accounts for edge singularities. The analysis technique is applied to a unit cell consisting of two sets of five parallel dipoles that are shifted one with respect to the other to create a Huygens resonance that maximizes transmission of the impinging plane wave. Comparisons with circuit models show that the proposed technique achieves better accuracy while providing significant computational gains compared with commercial general purpose software. Finally, a unit cell is optimized to work in the W band with the aim of employing it to the design of TAs for ultra-capacity fixed wireless links.

articleTitle: Ring Shape Helical Positioning Antenna With Tight Coupling Folded Arm in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This research proposed a compact, low-profile, lightweight quadrifilar and low-cost helix antenna for GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) positioning applications. It is achieved mass production and deployed in UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles). This antenna is especially suitable for lightweight equipment requirements scenarios. The tight coupling and multiple-branch are introduced in the design, to overcome the challenge from the bandwidth and geometry size. With four folded arms on the periphery of the ring shape holder, the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> band (1575.42±1.023 MHz) and L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> band (1227.60±1.023 MHz) are covered. This design balances the electric performance and the stability of the antenna. The antenna with 10 mm in height, 42 mm in diameter, and 10 grams in weight. The tested active gain reaches 30.3 dBi in the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> band, and 34.2 dBi in the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> band, which satisfies the high accuracy positioning requirements. The dynamic positioning accuracy tests demonstrated the antenna's performance and reliability.

articleTitle: An Estimation Method of Time Step Bound in DGTD for Periodic Structure Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The split-field scheme has been widely used in finite difference time domain (FDTD) method for the solution of periodic electromagnetic structures. In this letter, the split-field strategy has been extended to discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method for the first time, and the stability condition of the resulting method is analytically derived. An elementwise solution approach based on the matrix decomposition technique is further developed to improve the computational efficiency of time step bound estimation for both the normally and obliquely incident periodic boundary conditions (PBCs). Several numerical examples are given to demonstrate the good accuracy and the high efficiency of the proposed split-field DGTD method.

articleTitle: Multibeam 1-Bit Coding Programmable Metasurface Based on Superposition Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposed an algorithm utilizing the continuous phase superposition method to efficiently code multibeam 1-bit programable metasurface array. This method enables rapid metasurface array multibeam coding, which involves first calculating and superimposing the continuous phase matrix, and then the resulting code matrix is discretized. Additionally, an optimized algorithm is presented to lower the complexity of the overall procedure. The proposed algorithm enables the direct calculation of a maximum of 32 beam codes. The proposed algorithm exhibits high computational speed, low hardware resource consumption, and achieves high accuracy in generating beam pointing. The proposed algorithm addresses the issue of combining the number of beams, processing speed, and accuracy in the calculation of metasurface coding, which is not possible with standard algorithms. The algorithm is tested and validated using a 64 × 64 scale 1-bit metasurface array with meta-element full-wave simulation. During the test, 32 independent beams with arbitrary pointing directions are generated by the proposed algorithm. A maximum off-axis angle of 45° for the scanning range is supported by the proposed algorithm. Generated beams are both independent and clear, and the beam pointing error is limited to a maximum of 0.25%. The proposed algorithm for dual-beam coding achieves an average computation time of 1.18 ms, which is about 30 000 times faster than the typical nonlinear iterative optimization algorithm that takes 38 s.

articleTitle: An SISL All-FR4 Based Dual-Polarized Broadband High-Gain Antenna With Differential Open Feed Line for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A differential-fed dual-polarized antenna based on substrate-integrated suspended line (SISL) technology is proposed for millimeter-wave base stations. The differential feed structure is used to improve the port isolation and cross-polarization discrimination (XPD). It adopts the method of adding coupling patches as the load to improve impedance matching and obtain broadband performance without introducing additional structures, forming a two-unit antenna array to achieve high gain. An equivalent circuit model of the evolving antenna is analyzed. After changing the shape of the patch and adding branches, the bandwidth and gain were further improved. A pair of orthogonal differential open feed lines are utilized to realize dual polarization. The measured results show that the –10 dB bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 66.7% from 20 GHz to 40 GHz, and the 3 dB gain bandwidth is 67.8%. Port isolation is better than 40 dB, and XPD is better than 25 dB. In addition, the peak gain and radiation efficiency reached 8.7 dBi and 85%, respectively. The proposed antenna has the advantages of low cost, wide bandwidth, high gain, low cross polarization, high port isolation, etc.

articleTitle: A Waveform-Selective Antenna Loaded with A Nonlinear Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a waveform-selective antenna is proposed, which consists of a radiating patch antenna and a nonlinear circuit with two rectifier diodes. The waveform of the input signal can determine the operating state of the diodes, consequently, leading to reflecting/receiving signal response of the antenna. To illustrate the working mechanism, an equivalent circuit is established based on the simplified input source and diode resistance. For demonstration, a prototype of the antenna is fabricated. The measured results show that the antenna can work normally under continuous wave (CW) input, regardless of the input power, whose gain and radiation pattern are similar to those of a typical patch antenna. In contrast, the antenna performance will be affected by the input power when the input signal is a pulse wave (PW). At most 65% of PW power can be shielded when the input signal is of high power.

articleTitle: A Single-Feed Dual-Band Dual-Beam Filtering Patch Antenna With Concurrent CP and LP Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A single-feed dual-band dual-beam filtering patch antenna with both circular polarization (CP) and linear polarization (LP) properties is proposed in this letter. Dual bow-tie-shaped patches are used for concurrently achieving dual-beam and CP radiation in the lower passband. By employing L-shaped metal strips and a folded T-shaped stepped impedance feedline (FTSIF), the filtering response is introduced, simultaneously giving rise to the upper passband with LP operation. Additionally, through loading a T-shaped resonator, a deep radiation null (RN) is yielded between the two passbands. Consequently, dual-beam filtering responses with CP in the lower and LP in the upper passbands are, respectively, realized. For validation, a prototype is fabricated and tested. Two measured passbands operate at 5.30 GHz to 5.69 GHz and 6.11 GHz to 6.29 GHz, showing good dual-beam CP and LP radiation, respectively.

articleTitle: 270-GHz InP HBT Detector Modules Utilizing WR-3.4 Waveguide and Silicon Lens
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper introduces WR-3.4 waveguide and 3-mm diameter silicon lens modules, which house H-band InP detector integrated circuits (ICs). All detectors, including IC and modules, demonstrate excellent performance. The IC achieves a responsivity of 960 kV/W and a noise equivalent power (NEP) of 25 fW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup> at 270 GHz, aided by an active preamplifier that covers the entire H-band with over 20 dB gain. A free-space measurement method accurately assesses the lens module's radiation directivity. Despite losses arising from the feed antenna mismatch, leading to a relatively low packaging efficiency of 6.4%, the lens module still performs impressively, delivering a responsivity of 61 kV/W and an NEP of 394 fW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup> at 270 GHz.

articleTitle: Improving the Scanning Coverage of Array Antennas With Multilayer Lenses Designed With a Ray Tracing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Integrating dielectric lenses with phased array antennas can be beneficial in numerous applications, yet the design procedure typically requires significant computational effort. In this work, we employ a streamlined in-house 2-D ray-tracing model to design dielectric lenses, with the goal of enhancing the gain of an array antenna at large scanning angles. The ray-tracing model also accounts for losses from material absorption and reflections. The interfaces between the dielectric layers of these lenses devised in this study are defined using splines to allow a large flexibility of their shape. First, dielectric lenses consisting of a core layer supplemented by two matching layers are investigated. The results show better performance compared to the lens constructed using the conic equation. In addition, multilayer dielectric lenses also provide more flexibility, as proved by the proposed configuration with five layers which also minimizes reflections in the optimized direction. Finally, a nonuniform multilayer lens, featuring two layers on the sides and a single layer near to broadside can improve gain at 60$^\circ$ while maintaining efficiency at smaller angles.

articleTitle: Conformal Anisotropic Periodic Boundary Condition for FDTD Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel conformal periodic boundary condition (PBC) is proposed for the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method to accurately model anisotropic periodic structures. The conformal FDTD algorithms based on the effective material parameters are attractive due to their simplicity of implementation, but they require a reduced time step to maintain the Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy condition. In this letter, we introduce a novel conformal FDTD scheme for anisotropic materials. This scheme integrates the simplified conformal finite integration technique with the effective material parameters, which is not only simple to implement, but also avoids the time step reduction due to the effectively small cells. In addition, we extend this conformal algorithm toPBC to accurately simulate anisotropic periodic structures. Finally, to validate the proposed method's accuracy and efficiency, we present two illustrative examples.

articleTitle: Advancing Accuracy of SBR Method for RCS Prediction of Triangular Meshed Curved Targets Based on Curvature Wavefront Ray Tracing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A more accurate shooting and bouncing ray method (SBR) based on curvature wavefront ray tracing is proposed for radar cross section (RCS) simulation of triangular meshed curved targets. The key idea is to approximate the ray tube of each triangle using the wavefront of its center ray, thus accurately characterizing the divergence factor during multiple reflections. Surface fitting and differential geometry techniques are used to reconstruct the curvature of the triangular mesh and calculate the wavefront variations of the ray tube during multiple reflections, while also accounting for thin-coated targets. Moreover, a curvature wavefront-based ray tracing method is developed, significantly enhancing the sampling accuracy. The accuracy of the proposed SBR is validated through comparison with the FEKO multilevel fast multipole method (FEKO-MLFMM), and the simulation time consumption is acceptable.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Decoupling Method Using the Weak Radiation of SIW-to-Microstrip Transition for Millimeter-Wave Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A low profile, wideband decoupling technique utilizing the weak radiation of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)-to-microstrip transition is proposed in this letter. The transition serves as not only the feeding of an antenna element but also the key part for generating a decoupling path. By integrating with a metal plane beneath the transitions of two antenna elements, the weak radiation of the SIW-to-Microstrip transition can be extracted as an additional coupling path to achieve decoupling. This method is effective for both the E-plane and H-plane coupled antenna arrays. To explain the decoupling principle, equivalent circuits are established and analyzed. For demonstration purposes, H-plane and E-plane coupled twoelement antenna arrays working around 25 GHz are fabricated and measured. The results indicate that within the operation band, the mutual coupling is reduced to lower than –30 dB for Hplane and –25 dB for E-plane coupled antenna arrays. The proposed decoupling method features a simple design procedure, wide operating band, as well as low insertion loss.

articleTitle: A Novel Half-Apertured Multiplicative Array for Antenna Pattern Synthesis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Pattern synthesis is pivotal for designing antenna arrays to achieve expected radiation patterns, crucial in modern communication systems and sensing. Extremely large scale antenna arrays (ELAAs), which have gained significant interest for future wireless communication and sensing systems, has faced challenges in practice due to its complex and costly system architectures with massive antenna configuration and associated radio frequency (RF) chains. Multiplicative array (MA), which can achieve identical radiation pattern as the uniform rectangular array (URA) with much less antenna elements, is an established concept for array pattern synthesis. In this work, we introduce a novel half-apertured MA antenna pattern synthesis technique, which can achieve the same radiation pattern as the conventional MA (also same as the URA beamforming pattern) with only half the aperture of the MA design. It significantly reduces the required number of antenna elements and array aperture compared to URA and conventional MA while with no performance loss. Both numerical simulations and experimental validations have been performed to verify the effectiveness and flexibility of the proposed HMA. This innovation constitutes a significant advancement in MA design for pattern synthesis, offering promising applications in future research and implementations of large-scale arrays.

articleTitle: Phase-Only Beamforming for Dual-Polarization Array Radar Based on Manifold Optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The phase-only beamforming (POB) technique manipulates the weighted phases of array antenna elements to create a desired radiation pattern, thereby reducing the hardware and power costs associated with large phased arrays. However, two significant challenges currently hinder the practical implementation of POB. First, the beam gain generated by POB can be severely distorted when a main lobe interference is present. Second, the POB method struggles to suppress interferences whose positions change within the spatial domain. To address these challenges, this letter proposes a novel POB method for dual-polarization array radar. This method incorporates polarization constraints on a Riemannian manifold under the condition of null broadening. By doing so, it generates robust nulls that can effectively suppress moving interferences in the main lobe and side lobes while preserving the beam gain. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this method exhibits excellent anti-interference performance.

articleTitle: Efficient PWS-Based Computation of the Sensing Matrix for Computational Radar Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents an efficient method to compute the sensing matrix of computational imaging (CI) systems based on the plane wave spectrum (PWS) representation of electromagnetic waves. CI has recently been proposed as a promising paradigm to overcome some of the limitations of conventional radar imaging systems (mainly related to low acquisition speeds). As CI resorts to antennas that radiate spatially incoherent patterns to compress the scene information, the system complexity is transferred to the signal processing layer. CI systems are characterized by means of the so-called sensing matrix, which properly accounts for the spatially incoherent behavior of the antennas. The conventional method used to compute the sensing matrix is based on a point-by-point propagation between the aperture fields and the imaged scene, which is significantly time consuming. To address this limitation, this work proposes a PWS-based method, which enables to perform a plane-to-plane propagation. This results in a drastic improvement in the time required to compute the sensing matrix, without affecting its accuracy or the quality of the retrieved radar images. The proposed method has been experimentally validated with a CI system using frequency-diverse antennas.

articleTitle: A Fast Exponential Analysis and Variable Projection Based Method for Linear Array Synthesis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper presents a fast exponential analysis and variable projection method to reduce the number of elements in linear phased arrays. The numerical examples given in this work demonstrate a reduction of approximately 20% or 10% in the number of elements, with only a slight decrease in directivity of 0.63 dBi observed for a scan range of <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[-45^\circ,45^\circ ]$</tex-math></inline-formula>. Compared to the combined matrix pencil and Tabu search algorithm, the proposed technique converges in fewer iterations and exhibits <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 5$</tex-math></inline-formula> dB reduction in maximum side lobe level.

articleTitle: Compact Self-Diplexing MIMO Antenna with Improved Isolation for IoT Connectivity
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper proposes a cavity-backed substrate-integrated-waveguide dual-feed self-diplexing MIMO antenna for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. To implement a self-diplexing operation, the half-mode SIW cavity is loaded with a rectangular slot carved on the top metal cladding. This causes the cavity to be divided into two unequal apertures, resulting in the development of a quarter-mode SIW. The patch has orthogonally positioned feed lines that provide two distinct resonant frequencies, 5.18 GHz and 5.8 GHz, with respect to the fundamental mode <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$TE_{110}$</tex-math></inline-formula>. Employing metallic vias on the cavity improves the self-isolation between the orthogonal ports. Furthermore, a square aperture between orthogonal patches can achieve maximum isolation without additional units. The proposed compact MIMO antenna with a self-diplexing feature using an aperture slot achieves maximum isolation of 46.84 dB at 5.17 GHz and 42.76 dB at 5.8 GHz between patches, inter-port isolation of 28.6 dB at <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$f_{L}$</tex-math></inline-formula> and 27.6 dB at <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$f_{H}$</tex-math></inline-formula> among ports, an impedance bandwidth of 130 MHz (5.236 - 5.106 GHz) and 174 MHz (5.88 - 5.72 GHz), and high gain of 4.5 dBi, and 5.46 dBi was achieved at 5.17 GHz and 5.8 GHz, respectively. In addition, the MIMO antenna's performance metrics are envelope correlation coefficient <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$< $</tex-math></inline-formula> 0.01 and diversity gain <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$>$</tex-math></inline-formula> 9.9 dB was assessed. The proposed MIMO antenna's performance is evaluated through full-wave EM analysis and physical measurements of the fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: Antiambiguity Direction Finding by Harmonics' Amplitudes With Two-Element Time-Modulated Array
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel antiambiguity method is proposed to eliminate the mirror-image ambiguity generated in direction finding (DF) with the two-element time-modulated array based simply on harmonic amplitude. When the time delay of the two modulation sequences and the array element spacing satisfy a specific relationship, the amplitude difference between the <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ +\text{1}\text{st}$</tex-math></inline-formula> and the <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ -\text{1}\text{st}$</tex-math></inline-formula> harmonics shows monotonicity with the variation of the incident angle. Consequently, the incident angle can be estimated without the interference of mirror-image ambiguity, solely based on the amplitude–frequency measurement result. This method can be easily implemented by frequency sweeping devices. Therefore, the proposed method is beneficial to develop DF systems with low complexity and cost. Numeric simulations and experiment have been conducted to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Spaceborne Phased Arrays Using Tri-Ridge Evanescent Waveguide Antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A full-metal phased array, based on tri-ridge evanescent-fed choke antenna elements, providing simultaneous dual-circular polarizations is proposed in this letter.
