The full-metal design minimizes power losses at antenna level, reducing system complexity as compared to approaches that rely on the use of dielectric materials and require over-dimensioned arrays for comparable performance. The proposed radiating element enables very low coupling between orthogonally polarized input ports even when scanning. Therefore, this design supports wide-angle scanning in spaceborne phased arrays, while maintaining excellent active matching and active polarization isolation. The proposed concept allows the generation of two independent and simultaneous beams with orthogonal circular polarization from the same apertures. Experimental validation is provided with a <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\text{14 GHz}$</tex-math></inline-formula> prototype scanning up to <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\pm$</tex-math></inline-formula>60<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^\circ$</tex-math></inline-formula>, for Ku-band low Earth orbit receive payloads.

articleTitle: Discretize-Then-Optimize Approach to Real-Time Tropospheric Refractivity Inversion
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This study proposes a tomographic method for tropospheric refractivity estimation. Step-by-step numerical scheme for the parabolic equation is considered as a computational graph. The gradient required for efficient inversion is computed using the method of automatic differentiation. Instead of inverting a single static profile, the process of profile variation over time is simulated and tracked. Numerical experiments were conducted for various profiles, frequencies, and receiver antenna parameters. The results demonstrate the adequacy, high performance, and robustness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Broadband Stub-Loaded Integrated Filtering Antenna for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a broadband stub-loaded integrated filtering antenna with a simple structure for 2G/3G/4G/IMT base station applications. By adding stubs to the dipole arms, new current paths and radiation nulls are introduced, effectively suppressing the radiations outside the passband. Two L-shaped stubs with different lengths introduce controllable radiation nulls at out-of-band to achieve frequency-selective characteristics. Moreover, parasitic patch stubs surrounding the radiator serve to enhance the suppression level at high frequencies. The measured results indicate that impedance bandwidth is 65% and out-of-band suppression performance is more than 16 dB. Stable realized gain of around 8.4 dBi and high isolation of more than 25 dB are obtained within the passband. Moreover, the integrated controllable filtering performance has been validated with filtering antenna array for modern base station applications.

articleTitle: Synthesis Method for Low Ripple 1-D and 2-D Uniform Microwave Field via Spatial Spectrum Low-Pass Filtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Uniform microwave field (UMF) plays an important role in medical, industrial, and measurement in recent decades. It is a challenging problem to avoid Gibbs phenomenon in synthesizing UMF since the infinite spectrum component. In this letter, an analytical synthesis method based on spatial spectrum low-pass filtering is presented to shape low ripple UMF. The angular spectrum projection (ASP) principle is used as the foundation and combined with Fejer and Gauss–Weierstrass summation theory, which have better convergence than Fourier summation, to the reconstruction of low ripple UMF. Thereby, the proposed method not only keeps the analyticity of ASP but also has a better effect on reducing the ripple. Finally, several full-wave simulations are provided and the results demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Conical Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface with Frequency Response Stability
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a miniaturized conical bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) with excellent transmission performance stability for radome applications is proposed. The angular stability of the designed FSS structure in the planar state can reach 80°. Furthermore, when the FSS structure is conformal on a conical surface with a half-angle α of 30°, the resonant frequency shifts are less than 1.21% under both the x and y polarization. Finally, the FSS structure is fabricated and measured in the planar and conical states. The experimental results indicate that the angular stability of the conical FSS with a half-angle α of 41.9° can be up to 75°. A good agreement between the simulated and measured results verifies the effectiveness of the designed FSS.

articleTitle: Adaptive Receiver Orientation Intracavity Microwave Power Transfer Using Programmable Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In intracavity microwave power transfer (MPT) applications, receiver rotations cause fluctuations and a decrease in over-the-air (OTA) efficiency. To address this issue, we propose an intracavity MPT system incorporating metasurfaces that are programmable in both phase and polarization. Programmable metasurfaces (PMS) manipulate both the reflection phase and the polarization direction of microwaves within the cavity, thereby altering the electric field strength and polarization direction at the receiver. Subsequently, we develop an adaptive receiver orientation algorithm that integrates genetic algorithms with time reversal (TR) theory to optimize the PMS pattern. For experimental validation, an intracavity MPT system, incorporating 147 meta-atoms and operating at 2.4 GHz, was designed, fabricated, and tested. Experimental results indicate that our system achieved an improvement of at least 11 dB in the OTA efficiency, reaching an efficiency of 13% or more at the measurement orientation, compared to systems using a fixed PMS pattern. This improvement significantly enhances the robustness of the intracavity MPT system against variations in receiver orientation.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Controlling the Divergence Angle of Multimode Vortex Beams
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a new method for controlling the divergence angles of multimode orbital angular momentum (OAM) vortex beams. A geometric framework is established that allows for the same divergence angle across different OAM modes, which addresses a significant challenge in multimode systems. Proposed method combines 1-D linear array theory and the design of OAM beams with an equal divergence angle. By adjusting element phases, precise divergence control is achieved without altering the metasurface structure. The method's effectiveness is verified through theoretical synthesis, full-wave simulations, and experimental validation. This approach offers accurate control over a wide range of angles, demonstrating potential applications in communication systems.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Transmitarray Antenna Based on Differential Unit Cell
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a new differential receiving-transmitting (R-T) unit cell for a wideband circularly polarized transmitarray antenna (CPTA) is presented. The proposed unit cell consists of a rotational symmetric half U-slot patch (HUSP) pair for the receiving part and a two-arm spiral antenna for the transmitting part. The rotational symmetric HUSP pair generates the wideband differential currents. To produce high-gain CP directive radiation based on the phase compensation principle, a spatially dependent rotation angle is imposed on the transmitter, and a mirror symmetry is applied in the y-direction for the receiver to implement the required transmission phase. The proposed CPTA based on the designed element not only exhibits a wide measured 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 61.9% (15.5-29.4 GHz), but also yields a significant 3-dB gain bandwidth of 47.4% (17.7-28.7 GHz). In addition, the CPTA demonstrates an acceptable peak aperture efficiency (50.7%).

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wide-Angle Beam-Scanning Phased Array Based On Full-Wavelength Slot Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The phased array with wide scanning range is significant to increase signal coverage for millimeter-wave communication. In this letter, a millimeter-wave wide-angle beam-scanning phased array based on crossed full-wavelength slot elements is presented. High-gain performance of full-wavelength slot elements are used to improve the array boresight gain. The proposed crossed slot antenna element has a pair of mirror symmetrical radiating full-wavelength slots. The crossed slot is designed with parallel arms to reduce element-to-element distance for the phased array. Furthermore, parasitic slots are loaded in the vicinity of outer elements of the array to increase the element beamwidth. Due to small element spacing and wide-beam characteristic of outer elements, the beam-scanning angle of the millimeter-wave array is enhanced substantially. As a result, simulated and measured results show that the proposed 1×8 phased array has scanning angles of ±80° with 4-dB scan loss in 26.0-30.0 GHz. Compared with other related works, the proposed array has wider beam-scanning range with high gain and compact size.

articleTitle: Generalized Hole-Free Sparse Antenna Array Design With Even/Odd Maximum Interelement Spacing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we introduce two generalized sparse antenna arrays designed based on the maximum interelement spacing constraint (MISC) criterion. The proposed arrays, named GEMISC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub> and GEMISC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub>, are developed by filling the holes of enhanced MISC array (EMISC) through sensor rearrangement, with a special focus on even and odd maximum interelement spacings (MIES). The GEMISC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub> and GEMISC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O</sub> are constructed by configurating the interelement spacings (IES) set and are proved to possess filled difference coarrays. In addition, several common characteristics for the hole-free MISC-based array designs are outlined. Theoretical propositions and simulations validate the performance of the proposed arrays in terms of uniform degrees of freedom and mutual coupling, underscoring their potential to enhance target identifiability and estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized SIW-Based Scalable Antenna Array and 2-D Monopulse Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This article presents a SIW-based dual-polarized 2-D monopulse scalable antenna array in the millimeter-wave (MMW) scenario. To obtain similar radiation characteristics for dual polarization over a wide bandwidth, a symmetric magnetoelectric (ME) dipole cavity-backed antenna is designed. A <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbf{T}{{\mathbf{E}}_{140}}$</tex-math></inline-formula> mode feeding cavity is utilized to make the array scalable. The cascades of magic tees enable this dual-polarized array to achieve sum-difference beamforming in two dimensions. To validate our idea, a 4×4 antenna prototype was manufactured and tested. The measured overlapped bandwidth for eight ports reaches 23.02% (33.45 GHz-42.15 GHz). The gains of the sum, difference, and bi-difference beams reach 19.4 dBi, 16.1 dBi, and 13.4 dBi, and their null depths are greater than 31 dB.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Path Loss Prediction With Novel Diffraction and Morphology Features
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Several machine learning (ML) algorithms have been applied to predict path loss values, and various features have been proposed as input features in ML models. This study proposed two new types of features: diffraction parameter and morphology ratio features. In addition, we conducted a field measurement campaign to collect actual path loss data in various propagation environments. We conducted ablation studies on our own path loss dataset to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed features using various ML models. The results demonstrated that the prediction accuracy of each ML model improved when the proposed features were added to the input feature vector.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Array Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An ultrawideband horizontally polarized (HP) omnidirectional array antenna, characterized by superior out-of-roundness, is proposed in this letter. The array antenna comprises 16 radiating elements with a hybrid wide-angle impedance matching layer, a feed network, and a paraboloidal metal reflector. Specifically, three-order dipoles (TODs) are embraced as the radiating elements to obtain ultrawideband characteristics by adjusting the arm-length ratio of each order appropriately. Meanwhile, a compact feed network is designed in the center of the ring formed by radiating elements, ensuring uniform feeding for each element. Despite maintaining equal amplitude and phase in the feed, the array manifests out-of-roundness deterioration in the reference horizontal plane. To address this concern, a double-layer metal plate is introduced to form a paraboloidal reflector with the reference ground. This structure eliminates the ripples of the radiation pattern, thereby effectively enhancing the out-of-roundness. A prototype is fabricated and measured. The proposed antenna achieves a 4.0:1 operating bandwidth and exhibits excellent omnidirectional pattern characteristics, with out-of-roundness in the horizontal plane less than 1 dB throughout the full operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Vertically Polarized Endfire Leaky-Wave Antenna With Flexible Control of Propagation Constants
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a vertically polarized endfire leaky-wave antenna (LWA) by periodically loading shunt inductive cavity at two sides of the double-sided parallel strip line. Different from most of nonuniform LWA with matched phases at a single frequency, the proposed one can realize the matched phase constants in the operating band with adjusted attenuation constant values along antenna for certain distributions. The structural influences are investigated to explore the proper loading configuration to meet the requirements for the propagation constants. It is found that the widths of the inductive loading cavity and its connecting line can be employed to control the attenuation constants obviously with weak effects on phase values and slopes in the operation band. In this way, a nonuniform prototype antenna with Taylor distribution is designed to prove its ability of flexibly control propagation constants in the operation range. The simulated results agree well with the measured ones, which confirms the merits of the proposed loading strategy in realizing some specific radiation performances.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Circularly Polarized Filtering Slot Antenna Based on Stub-Loaded Resonators
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel approach to designing a highly selective circularly polarized (CP) filtering antenna. It is based on rectangular waveguide cavity resonators that are directly coupled to each other. Capacitive stubs are loaded onto the cavity ends without increasing the circuit size to create adjustable transmission nulls. Two orthogonal radiating slots are opened onto the side-wall of the last coupled resonator to achieve end-fire CP radiation. An equivalent circuit model is presented to analyze the numerical results. The approach is eventually demonstrated by designing, simulating, and fabricating a fourth-order CP filtering antenna operating at X-band. The measured and simulated results are in excellent agreement, showing a quasi-elliptic response with a gain value of 7.0 ± 0.1 dBic over the passband. The 10-dB reflection coefficient (S11) and 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths are 7.5% and 5.5%, respectively. The competitive performance and compactness of the proposed device make it a promising candidate for stringent frequency selectivity applications.

articleTitle: 3-D Forward Parametric Model for Strong Coupling Scattering from Complex Cavities
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter provides a forward parametric model to obtain strong coupling scattering from metallic cavities accurately. To evaluate the coupling scattering effectively, optical path difference equivalence method and parametric extraction are proposed. Firstly, the rays are transformed into 3-D equivalent reflection points during ray tracing based on an alternative optical path difference equivalence method. Then, the parameters of the attributed scattering center model can be extracted based on forward modeling methods. The alternative optical path difference equivalence method aims to transform the coupling scattering within the cavity into a more simplified form, thereby facilitating concise parametric extraction. The accuracy is validated through numerical simulations of cavity models.

articleTitle: Optimized UWB Antenna Deployment Based on Improved Equalization Optimizer Algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) localization accuracy is influenced by the deployment spacing of base stations, and suboptimal deployment patterns can impede optimal localization performance. To address this challenge, we propose a UWB base station deployment spacing optimization strategy based on the PLD-EO algorithm. The PLD-EO algorithm integrates piecewise map, Lévy flight, and dynamic reverse learning to effectively balance local development and global search. Initially, a localization quality control model is established, with fuzzy parameters determined through UWB antenna ranging tests conducted in natural environments. Subsequently, we compared the convergence of 12 algorithms in solving the model. The results indicate that the PLD-EO algorithm exhibits the fastest convergence speed in addressing the control model. Finally, the PLD-EO algorithm is successfully applied to determine the optimal deployment distance of the antenna within the stable area of the ultra-wideband signal.

articleTitle: Channel Emulation for Dynamic Channel Models with Programmable Turntable in OTA Testing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Dynamic channel models are under extensive investigation to provide a more accurate modeling of varying interaction between wireless transceivers and propagation environments. On the other hand, the existing channel emulation methods for over-the-air (OTA) testing were designed for spatially-static channel models. In this letter, we propose a novel method for dynamic channel emulation by utilizing the ability of the programmable turntable to adjust the orientation of the device-under-test (DUT) during OTA testing. Thanks to the additional degree-of-freedom provided by the programmable turntable, more favorable angular positions between the DUT and the OTA probe antennas can be dynamically obtained to cater for the instantaneous channel multipath directions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy of dynamic channel emulation, which exhibits strong feasibility even under the practical constraint of turntable rotation speed.

articleTitle: Wideband Superstrate-Loaded Metasurface-based Multifunctional Polarization Converters
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, two different configurations of a multifunctional polarizer are designed in a compact geometry for simultaneous linear-to-circular (LP-to-CP) and linear-to-linear (LP-to-LP) polarization conversion with enhanced bandwidths. The metasurface unit cell consists of an anisotropic geometry printed on a metal-backed dielectric substrate, while a superstrate is placed above the pattern to aid in the bandwidth enhancement. The configuration-1 exhibits simultaneous wideband LP-to-LP conversion in the range of 4.52-4.76 GHz, 7.94-15.95 GHz, as well as wideband LP-to-CP conversion over 4.90-7.41 GHz, 16.12-16.97 GHz. Subsequently, the characteristic mode analysis is utilized to modify the design topology, and Configuration-2 is realized with multi-band LP-to-LP conversion at 4.73-5.09 GHz, 6.58-7.66 GHz, and simultaneous wideband LP-to-CP conversion over 5.36-6.12 GHz, 8.08-15.02 GHz. Both designs have small footprints (having unit cell dimensions of 0.143λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.143λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> being the lowest operating wavelength) and demonstrate angularly stable characteristics up to 50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> incidence. The structures are fabricated and the experimental responses are in good agreement with the simulations. Later, two checkerboards (CB-1 and CB-2) using two different metasurface configurations are designed, leveraging their phase gradient responses for low radar cross-section (RCS) applications, depicting >10 dB RCS reduction bandwidths over 4.5-4.8 GHz, 7.9-16.1 GHz for CB-1, and 4.8-5.3 GHz, 7.0-7.7 GHz for CB-2, respectively.

articleTitle: An Efficient Reactive Near-Field Measurement Method for Active Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Near-field measurements of active phased array antennas are typically carried out in the radiation region several wavelengths away from the antennas. The reactive near field distributed on the antenna surface carries high-resolution information, which is suitable for the array element measurement. However, limited by the aperture size of the conventional near-field probe (such as the open-ended waveguide), it is unable to obtain the high-resolution reactive near-field distribution of the active phased antennas. In this letter, we propose an efficient reactive near-field measurement method utilizing scanning optic-induced plasma scattering technology. A Ka-band active transmitting phased array antenna was measured. This method enables the direct observation of reactive near-field distributions with high resolution, allowing for high-efficiency measurement of the antenna operational states in tens of seconds. It is demonstrated that the proposed method can achieve the reactive near-field measurement efficiently and has significant potential for applications in antenna array diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna Using Tunable Band-Stop FSS With Reduced Switching Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter details the design of a compact pattern-reconfigurable antenna that is based on the analysis of a tunable gap-incorporated band-stop frequency selective surface (FSS) unit cell. By changing the state of the RF PIN diode, the proposed FSS unit cell can demonstrate either a dipole-resonance mode or a circulating-current mode, thus allowing it to behave as a reflective or transparent structure, respectively, around the same frequency. A simple pattern-reconfigurable antenna with reduced active switching elements for omnidirectional and directional beam-steering that is created by utilizing the proposed FSS unit cell can fulfill the desired function while avoiding the complexities involved in employing large FSS arrays. A prototype of the proposed antenna is fabricated and measured, and it shows a return loss |S11| < –10 dB from 1.7 GHz to 1.8 GHz, along with a peak gain of 6.8 dBi. Ultimately, this proposed antenna is expected to be applicable in various wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Wideband Omnidirectional Metasurface Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A wideband omnidirectional metasurface antenna has been proposed. The characteristic mode analysis (CMA) was applied to explore the modal behaviors of the metasurface and guide the design. The proposed metasurface is designed based on a 5 × 5 square patched array, which is a hybrid metasurface incorporating square patches with 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 subarrays in a distributive arrangement, significantly improving the bandwidth and current distribution over a wide band. By properly adjusting the sizes of these elements, the bandwidth and gain are further improved. Based on the predicted excitation of the metasurface, a probe center-fed circular patch is introduced on the bottom layer, which not only excites the metasurface but also generates an additional mode to compensate the metasurface for attaining stable omnidirectional radiation. An antenna prototype was simulated, fabricated, and tested. The results show that the proposed antenna achieves a wide bandwidth of 70.1%, a peak gain ranging from 2 dBi to 6 dBi, and radiates a good omnidirectional pattern.

articleTitle: A Broadband Ultralow Reflection Absorber Based on Complementary Pairs With Multiresonant Units
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A broadband ultralow reflection frequency selective surface absorber is proposed based on a novel multiresonant unit, leveraging the advantages of complementary pairs for impedance matching. The equivalent circuit model of the proposed multiresonant unit is presented and analyzed to elucidate the mechanism behind the four resonant states that facilitate broadband absorption. The operating bandwidth is further increased by incorporating a complementary layer into the multiresonant unit while maintaining a consistent total thickness for the absorber. Three complementary pairs with the same unit but different parameters are introduced sequentially to reduce reflection, and the Y-Smith chart is provided to illustrate the progressively stringent impedance matching. The proposed absorber achieves a reflection coefficient of less than <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-20$</tex-math></inline-formula> dB from 2.24 GHz to 15.8 GHz, resulting in a fractional bandwidth of 150.3%. Furthermore, the reflection coefficient remains below <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-10$</tex-math></inline-formula> dB at oblique incidence angles of up to <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\text{60}^\circ$</tex-math></inline-formula>. A prototype consisting of <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\text{30} \times \text{30}$</tex-math></inline-formula> units was fabricated and measured, with the results showing good agreement with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Conforming Discretization Based on Characteristic Basis Function for Magnetic Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The dual testing scheme using the Buffa–Christiansen (BC) basis function not only maintains the good convergence of the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) but also improves its accuracy. However, in practical applications, fewer unknowns are desired to reduce the computing resources of the nBC-tested MFIE. In this letter, a novel conforming discretization based on characteristic basis functions (CBFs) is proposed to mitigate the problem of the conventional nBC-tested MFIE. The proposed discretization can acquire a well-conditioned discretization of the identity operator leading to a satisfactory iterative convergence while keeping a conforming testing scheme. The resulting system matrix is smaller than the original system matrix of the conventional nBC-tested MFIE while inheriting satisfactory iterative convergence and accuracy. Numerical results are shown to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Compact and Low-Profile High-Gain Multilayer Vivaldi Antenna Based on Gradient Metasurface Superstrates
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents the design, analysis, and implementation of an electrically compact high-gain multilayer Vivaldi antenna. The multilayer antenna comprises gradient metasurface superstrate layers arranged on the top and bottom of a central electrically compact Vivaldi antenna via low-loss polyethylene foam spacers. The overall electrical dimensions of the antenna are 0.36λ0 x 0.29λ0 x 0.06λ0, covering a bandwidth from 450 MHz to 10 GHz with an average measured forward gain of more than 15 dBi (λ0: free space wavelength at 450 MHz). The unit pixel dimensions of the gradient metasurface layer have been optimized to achieve a high-flat gain profile within the desired bandwidth of the antenna. The metasurface layers are printed on thin Kapton polyimide boards to minimize the system's weight. The prototyped antenna is extremely low-profile and weighs 182 grams, making it ideally suited for lightweight UWB applications needing a very high forward gain.

articleTitle: Generation of Reconfigurable Multimode OAM Waves Based on Single-Mode Array Multiplexing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel antenna design for generating multimode orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves through single-mode array multiplexing. The design consists of four single-mode primary uniform circular arrays (PUCA), each comprising four circularly polarized (CP) antenna elements sequentially rotated by 90°. These PUCAs are arranged in concentric circles, forming a 16-element quasi-UCA. By selectively exciting specific antenna elements using a simple feeding network with PIN diodes, different sequential rotation states can be achieved, enabling the generation of OAM waves in modes 0, 1, and −1. The designed feeding network, which avoids complex phase shifters, utilizes a straightforward element selection mechanism for flexible mode reconfigurability. Both simulations and measurements confirm high mode purity, exceeding 82% for all modes. This design offers an innovative solution for generating multi-mode OAM waves, with the advantages of low complexity, flexible control, and a compact profile.

articleTitle: Low-Profile, Broadband and High-Gain Circularly Polarized Endfire Antenna Design Employing Double-Crossover Offset Striplines
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a low-profile, broadband and high-gain circularly polarized endfire antenna design using a double- crossover offset stripline structure. It employs an alternating horizontal and vertical crossover configuration, where horizontal crossover structures produce horizontally polarized endfire radiation and vertical crossover ones lead to vertically polarized endfire radiation. By carefully tuning the magnitudes and phase difference of the two polarizations, one achieves circularly polarized endfire radiation using this simple low-profile antenna. A prototype with a small size of <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$5.14\lambda _{0}\times 0.06\lambda _{0}\times 0.05\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula> is designed, and experimental results show that the circularly polarized endfire radiation works within 10.6-11.15GHz (with a relative bandwidth of 5.1%). The measured average endfire gain is 10.6 dBic, and the measured efficiency is 71.7%.

articleTitle: Generation of Circularly Polarized Vortex Electromagnetic Waves Using a ME Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized (CP) vortex antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) with magnetoelectric (ME) dipole structure is proposed. A ME-structured CP antenna was first designed. It was then rotated and placed sequentially as an element to form an eight-element uniform circular array (UCA), which ultimately generated an electromagnetic wave carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM). An X -shaped slot, four square patches and four metallic vias form the ME structure. They are distributed on one side of the SIW structure, allowing the electric and magnetic dipoles to simultaneously contribute to the formation of the CP wave. The beam generated by the vortex antenna composed of ME elements has a good symmetry and vortex effect. After measurement, the highest mode purity of <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol{l=-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula> at 150mm from the vortex antenna is more than 90%, and the highest gain reaches more than 8 dBi.

articleTitle: Anomaly Correction for Radiation Patterns of Active Phased Array Antenna Based on a Neural Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Anomaly interference in the radiation pattern of an active phased array antenna (APAA) is an intractable problem, that affects the overall system performance. To overcome this problem, this paper proposes an antenna radiation pattern anomaly correction model (ARPACM) based on a neural network to compensate for the shortcomings of the antenna radiation pattern (ARP) under anomalous conditions. In addition, to overcome the problem of the scarce data, this study uses simulated anomalous ARPs that are consistent with practical experimental conditions to construct and train a pre-trained model, named simulated ARPACM (SARPACM). The weights of the last hidden layer of the SARPACM are optimized using experimental data by introducing transfer learning, yielding an optimized ARPACM. Extensive experiments are conducted to verify the proposed ARPACM. The results indicate that the proposed model can outperform widely used correction algorithms and other training strategies, in terms of a mean coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), a mean square error (MSE), a mean relative error (MRE), achieving improvements of 99.76%, 0.08 dB, and 1.29%, respectively. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate that the ARPACM can effectively correct the anomalies of ARPs caused by various interfering factors.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Multiband Shared-Aperture Antenna Using Multiplexed Metasurface
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces a multiband low-profile antenna by developing a simple metasurface (MS) and a hybrid feeding. The MS is reused as both a radiator for the y-polarized antenna and an artificial magnetic conductor reflector for the x-polarized antenna, resulting in a low profile of 0.1λ at 3.5 GHz through effective stacking. The y-polarized antenna takes the form of an MS-based grid-slotted patch with a wide band of 4.03 GHz to 5.63 GHz (1.6 GHz, 33.1%), while the x-polarized antenna is configured as a dipole with dual bands of 3.36 GHz to 3.70 GHz (0.34 GHz, 9.6%) and 5.14 GHz to 5.58 GHz (0.44 GHz, 8.2%). A defected ground structure is introduced to achieve impedance matching and generate a band notch for the dipole antenna. To address the misalignment of radiation patterns in the high-frequency band of the x-polarized antenna, an asymmetrical slot is employed for pattern correction by 11o.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Wideband Three-Reflector Compact Antenna Test Range System Based on Integrated Computational Electromagnetic Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we concentrate on computational electromagnetic modeling for a wideband three-reflector compact antenna test range (CATR) system and evaluate the subsequent quiet zone (QZ) field electromagnetic characteristics. The fast design of the feedhorn is accomplished by integrating a coarse model, employing the mode matching method and Stratton–Chu formula, with a high-fidelity model based on full-wave simulations. The reflectors are synthesized by integrating ray tracing and B-spline surface construction. The designed feed horn, in conjunction with two shaped sub-reflectors, forms a dual reflector feed system to complete the illumination of the main reflector. The QZ field for the three-reflector CATR is calculated using physical optics and the physical theory of diffraction in GRASP10. Utilizing Lorentz reciprocity theorem and plane wave spectrum, numerical calculations of far-field pattern measurement predictions are provided for three-reflector CATR and antenna-under-test combinations. The useful bandwidth of the three-reflector CATR is 480 GHz to 600 GHz, with a QZ diameter of approximately 1 m to 2 m. The copolar amplitude and phase ripple meet the quality criteria, and cross-polarization isolation exceeds 50 dB.

articleTitle: Novel OAM Antenna Based on Circular SIW Resonant Cavity
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In a communication system, orbital angular momentum (OAM) serves as a means for multichannel transmission, enhancing both transmission capacity and communication speed. A novel approach by integrating eight “L”-shaped slots as disturbance elements is proposed in this paper. The circular arrangement induces a phase difference across the antenna's surface, effectively replacing the need for a phase-controlled array. Each disturbance element functions akin to an array element, generating continuous phase-differing electromagnetic waves at an azimuthal angle. The antenna is designed with a single port, enabling the formation of the l = −1 mode, thereby significantly simplifying the OAM generation device. By leveraging a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) the antenna's footprint and cost are substantially reduced. Within the 22.7 GHz to 25.5 GHz frequency band, the antenna exhibits remarkable performance metrics: the modal purity of the l = −1 mode can reach over 95%, with a gain of over 8.2 dBi and a null depth of less than 40 dB. Additionally, it features a low profile, low cost, and high purity across a wide bandwidth, providing an ideal choice for wireless communication and radar technology.

articleTitle: Wearable Circularly Polarized SIW Antenna for Off-body Communications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A compact low-profile circularly polarized Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Antenna for off-body communications is proposed. The antenna is made of felt and conductive fabric to have good wearability. An annulus slot and four rectangular slots are etched on a circular SIW to adjust and combine the TM11 mode of the circular patch with the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> mode of the SIW resonant cavity, thereby achieving broadband. To achieve circular polarization, an inclined 45 ° rectangular slot is etched on the circular patch. The measured -3 dB Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth is 240 MHz (5.31 GHz -5.56 GHz). The average gain in the working band is 7.76 dBi. The low Specific Absorption Ratio (SAR) results also demonstrate that the radiation of the antenna to the human body is within the safe range.

articleTitle: Design of Microwave Ablation Antenna for Flexible Omnidirectional/Directional Ablation Zone Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a structure that can flexibly regulate omnidirectional/directional ablation zones is proposed. By fine-tuning the electrical length of tri-reflector, both ablation zones can be regulated in a similar antenna structure. Two prototypes were fabricated and tested: one for generating an omnidirectional ablation zone and the other for generating a directional ablation zone. Ablation experiments were performed in ex vivo porcine liver to observe the effects of different ablation times and reflector geometries on the antenna heating pattern. When the ablation lasted for 3 minutes at an input power of 20 W, the omnidirectional MWA antenna created a symmetric ablation zone of 22 mm × 19 mm with an aspect ratio of 91%; the directional MWA antenna generated an asymmetric ablation zone of 23 mm × 13 mm, with minimal heating occurring behind the reflector (< 2 mm) and a directivity ratio of 83.3%, which is significantly improved compared with the traditional method. This experiment validated the feasibility and effectiveness of the algorithm to control the ablation zone, providing a promising approach for designing other MWA antennas.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Frequency-Reconfigurable Dual-Polarized Patch Antenna Based on Fundamental Modes
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a dual-band, dual-polarized antenna design through the excitation of fundamental modes in both bands. The antenna employs a square patch integrated with four reactive stubs, which serve as capacitive loadings at low frequencies to lower the resonant frequency and make the antenna compact. Simultaneously, the stubs exhibit inductive properties exciting another fundamental mode of stable radiation at the high band. Additionally, frequency tunability is extended to dual-band operation maintaining the high isolation between dual polarizations. The fabricated prototype covers the frequency ranges of 2.3-2.49 GHz and 5.05-5.95 GHz, with a compact size of 27.5 × 27.5 × 4.8mm<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{3}$</tex-math></inline-formula>. The peak realized gain ranges from 4.8 to 7 dBi, and the isolation between the dual polarizations exceeds 30 dB across the operating frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Triplexer Antenna with High Isolation for BeiDou Communication and Navigation Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In response to insufficient isolation of microstrip triplexers, this work presents a design method for a tri-band antenna integrated with a passive triplexer. Based on the analytic resonant characteristics of stepped impedance resonators (SIRs), the combination of SIR and transmission lines is used to meet the impedance conditions required by the common junction of the triplexer. It has a simple structure, straightforward design equations, and high layout flexibility. A shorting pin is used to directly cascade the triplexer with a tri-band antenna, realizing the single PCB integration of the triplexer, antenna element, and feeding structure. Focusing on the application requirements of Beidou communication and navigation systems, a circularly polarized triplexer antenna with isolation greater than 52 dB between the transmitting and receiving ports is proposed.

articleTitle: An Accuracy-Enhanced Vector Fitting Technique and Its Applications to Model Electromagnetic Parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An accuracy-enhanced vector fitting (VF) technique is proposed in this letter to fit electromagnetic parameters, which do not require conjugate symmetric complex terms. Based on the original VF technique, a gain coefficient is introduced by each term in the pole-residue model and solved using the system equation constructed from measured data. Then, these coefficients are incorporated into the residual and constant of the corresponding term in the existing pole-residue model. In addition, four adaptive order selection schemes for engineering applications are discussed and given. Two numerical examples, including complex refractive index and relative permittivity of metals, and the surface conductivity of mulilayer graphene, demonstrate the improvement on the fitting accuracy of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual Port Circularly Polarized MIMO Antenna for On-/Off-Body WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a novel compact dual port circularly polarized multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for On-/Off-Body wireless body area network (WBAN) applications is proposed, radiating unidirectional and omnidirectional radiation patterns by two ports, respectively. By adding a circular arrangement of multiple shorting pins, the frequency points of the TM01/TM02 hybrid mode and TM11 mode of the circular patch are adjusted to the same frequency band, which are used as the resonant mode of two ports, respectively. In order to achieve circular polarization at the unidirectional port, a rectangular slot is etched in the center of the patch by bypassing the omnidirectional radiation port, and two rectangular slots are etched at the edge of the patch. The omnidirectional bandwidth is 70 MHz (3.45 GHz-3.52 GHz), and the unidirectional bandwidth is 190 MHz (3.41 GHz-3.6 GHz). By integrating a decoupling method based on characteristic mode analysis with circularized polarization, not only high port isolation was achieved but also communication degrees of freedom for the unidirectional mode was enhanced, making it suitable for a wider range of applications.

articleTitle: All-Metal Broadband Low-Profile Dual-Frequency Dual Circularly Polarized Aperture-Shared Antenna for Spaceborne Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this paper, an all-metal aperture-shared antenna (ASA) is demonstrated, which has the characteristics of low profile, broadband, dual frequency band, and dual circular polarization. ASA consists of one L-band antenna (LA) unit with four S-band antenna (SA) units surrounding LA unit, and the profile height is only 0.067 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>. The -10dB impedance & 3dB axial ratio bandwidth of ASA in S band and L band are 2.73 GHz∼3.37 GHz (21.0%) and 1.22 GHz∼1.71 GHz (33.4%), respectively. Considering the temperature fluctuations in the spaceborne application environments, the stability of antenna performance with temperature changes has also been analyzed. To verify the design method, an ASA prototype has been fabricated and measured, and the measured results agree well with the simulated ones, showing a great potential in the field of spaceborne phased arrays.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Dipole Filtenna With Grid-Shaped Radiator Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a dual-polarized broadband filtenna (filtering antenna) using grid-shaped transmission line as the radiator arm. It contains a grid-shaped dipole radiator, four impedance matching patches (IMPs), a metal loop and four C-shaped branches. The grid-shaped transmission line is used to replace the conventional dipole radiator for obtaining an upper band edge high frequency selectivity radiation null. Four IMPs are added to improve the antenna impedance matching. A metal loop and four C-shaped branches are introduced to generate specific out-of-band radiation nulls to ensure a high frequency selectivity and high suppression level. As a result, bandpass-type filtering radiation performance and high roll-off-rate response are obtained with three controllable radiation nulls. For demonstration, a prototype of the filtenna is manufactured and measured. The impedance bandwidth of the proposed filtenna is 54.5% (2.83∼4.95 GHz). The average measured realized gain is 7.8 dBi. Three radiation nulls and better than 19 dB out-of-band suppression levels are realized.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile and Low-Cost Metal-Only Folded Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A metal-only folded transmitarray antenna (MOFTA) with low-profile, low-cost, and high-gain is proposed in this letter. It consists of three parts, namely a top transmission surface (TS), a bottom reflection surface (RS), and a pyramidal horn as feed. All of three parts are made by metal, which could be cost effective and more tolerant for stringent surroundings. By embedding the feed horn in the bottom RS and together with the top TS, the profile of the proposed MOFTA is reduced to 1/3 of the focal length of the conventional transmitarray. The novelty of this letter is the successful design and implementation methodology of the entire MOFTA structure, which to the best of authors' knowledge has not been fully characterized and experimentally verified in the literature yet. According to results from experiments, it can realize 1-dB gain bandwidth of 10% and peak aperture efficiency of 42%. These appealing characteristics make the designed MOFTA very suitable for a wide range of high-gain applications.

articleTitle: A Mixed Discretization Scheme for Discontinuous Galerkin Domain Decomposition Method Applied to Surface Integral Equations
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The discontinuous Galerkin (DG)-based domain decomposition method has been proposed for analyzing complex electromagnetic scattering problems. For targets involving material regions, the electric (J) and magnetic (M) current combined field integral equation (JMCFIE) is often used. Since JMCFIE integrates first- and second-kind Fredholm integral equations, its accuracy is lower compared to the one using only first-kind integral equations. To address this issue, this letter studies a mixed discretization scheme for the DG-JMCFIE, using Buffa–Christiansen (BC) functions and Rao–Wilton–Glisson (RWG) functions as testing functions. For the first time, we provide explicit formulations for BC functions on the boundaries of DG subdomains. We also introduce a novel interior penalty method to weakly enforce current continuity across subdomain boundaries within the BC-RWG mixed discretization scheme. Numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the accuracy and convergence of our proposed method.

Author Keywords: electric and magnetic current combined field integral equations (JMCFIE)

articleTitle: A New Efficient Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Implantable Patch Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A dual-band, circularly polarized, highly efficient antenna for wireless power transfer applications in implanted devices is presented. Based on a modified square patch in microstrip technology of low profile and weight, the model presents operation in the frequency bands 915 MHz and 2.45 GHz. A study of the geometry is carried out to adjust the operating ranges of circular polarization in both frequencies, considering the environment with dispersive tissues. The proposed antenna exhibits improved efficient values compared to those of works reported in the literature, between 0.57% and 1.12%. The investigation of the specific absorption rate (SAR) and the operating power capacity is carried out. A prototype is fabricated and measured to validate the proposed design.

articleTitle: A High Gain Low SAR Wearable Antenna Based on AMC in Wireless Body Area Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A wearable dual-band antenna consisting of a ring radiating unit and an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is designed in wireless body area network (WBAN), and the substrate material chosen is felt, which is easy to bend and wear. The simulated maximum broadband gains are 6 dBi and 8.2 dBi at 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz, respectively, and the simulated maximum specific absorption rate (SAR) are 0.368W/kg and 0.222 W/kg, which are much lower than the international standards. The deformation analysis shows that the antenna can be used in the curved case and matches the performance in the planar case. The overall antenna fabrication process is simple, the experimental results and simulation results are basically consistent, and the designed antenna shows a high degree of consistency in free environment and simulated human body environment. The flexible antenna designed in this paper is expected to be applied to wireless wearable communication systems.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Wideband Metasurface Antenna Using Fully Multiplexed Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A fully multiplexed metasurface (FMMTS) is presented and exploited to engineer a low-profile, compact, and wideband metasurface antenna (MTA). The proposed FMMTS element is constructed by slotting and subdividing a conventional hexagonal radiating patch into three congruent diamond-shaped segments, with each one being shared by adjacent elements. This full-reusing configuration drastically enhances spatial efficiency. Additionally, the increased inter-unit gaps lead to supplementary edge capacitances, which effectively lower the resonance frequency of the FMMTS radiator, allowing for a more compact radiation aperture. Then, the FMMTS array is modified for miniaturization, and the characteristic mode analysis is adopted to explain its mechanism. As a proof of concept, the modified FMMTS array is coupled to a T-shaped feeding network through a rectangular aperture, forming a linearly polarized MTA and realizing an impressive impedance bandwidth of 57.83% and a peak gain of 6.93 dBi, all within an extremely compact overall size of 0.34λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> × 0.34λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> × 0.035λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> is the lower operating wavelength in free space), which shows a size reduction of approximately 50% when compared to recently developed wideband MTAs.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Independent Dual Linear Polarization Reflectarray Filtenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile dual-linear polarization reflectarray filtenna with a unit cell featuring a dual-polarization magneto-electric (ME) dipole based on split-ring resonators (SRRs). The ME dipole has two independent feeding sections, each connected to a separate open-ended microstrip line, enabling independent control of dual-polarization reflection phases. The ME dipole and SRRs generate low and high frequency radiation nulls, respectively. The filtenna achieves 3dB gain bandwidths of 19.3% for x-polarization and 18.5% for y-polarization, with maximum gains of 21.77dBi (35.1% efficiency) for x-polarization and 21.93dBi (36.4% efficiency) for y-polarization. The selectivity characteristics for x- and y-polarizations are 0.5 and 0.52, respectively. With a relative thickness of only 0.072λ, this filtenna is suitable for long-distance communication systems requiring high-capacity data transmission and integration.

articleTitle: A Broadband, High-Efficiency, Low-Sidelobe Transmitarray Antenna Employing Hybrid Transmission Metasurface Polarizer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A broadband, high efficiency transmitarray antenna (TA) with low sidelobe levels is proposed. First, an array antenna pattern synthesis algorithm is employed to predict and optimize the TA's radiation performance. Then, a novel set of hybrid metasurface elements is introduced, improving transmission bandwidth and efficiency compared to conventional single meta-atom designs, without increasing fabrication complexity. These elements maintain an average transmission coefficient exceeding 0.94 and offer 360° phase coverage from 8 GHz to 16 GHz (relative bandwidth of 66.7%). A TA prototype with a 186 mm aperture diameter was fabricated, exhibiting a measured peak gain of 24.35 dBi, a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 60.5%, and a peak aperture efficiency of 55.4%. Moreover, within this 3 dB gain bandwidth, the average sidelobe level is approximately −22.1 dB.

articleTitle: A Dual DNNs Method for Real-Time Beam Scanning and Stabilization of Deformed Conformal Array Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a method utilizing dual deep neural networks (DNNs) for real-time beam stabilization and scanning capability restoration in deformed conformal array antenna. Initially, the physical-driven deep neural networks based on active element pattern (AEP) are trained to swiftly generate the phase for directional control. Based on the pre-trained neural networks, the physical-driven deep neural networks semidefinite relaxation (PDNNs-SDR) algorithm is proposed to generate the amplitude that meets the requirements of the desirable radiation pattern. The data-driven deep neural networks are subsequently employed to achieve real-time amplitude output based on the existing amplitude as training data. Simulation and measured results demonstrate that the proposed methods can rapidly output the amplitude and phase corresponding to the desired radiation pattern. It combines the advantages of deep neural networks and convex optimization algorithm and achieves a good trade-off between both methods.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Polarized Meta-Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A broadband dual-polarized meta-dielectric resonator antenna (MDRA) array with high isolation is presented in this letter. The MDRA consists of the 4×4 meta-dielectric resonator (MDR) elements which can generate two resonant modes for the broadband operation. The side length of each MDR element is about 0.104λ0 (λ0 is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency) and its height is 0.132λ0. The cross-slot and two orthogonal microstrip feed networks are adopted to obtain the dual-polarized operation. To achieve high gain for the practical applications, the MDRA is arranged to form a 2×2 array. To verify the design, the MDRA array is fabricated and measured. The measurement results show the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 57.4% for the H-polarization and 57.7% for the V-polarization, the isolation of more than 29.5 dB and stable radiation pattern at the operation band. The proposed MDRA array will be an important candidate scheme for future broadband communication applications.

articleTitle: High-Order Mode Antenna with Pattern Reconfigurability for Intelligent IoT Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-gain, high-order-mode-based pattern reconfigurable antenna designed for intelligent wireless applications. To achieve a higher gain, a high-order mode slot radiator is employed. Then, by manipulating the field distributions of the long slot, different excitation modes are activated, leading to the development of a novel high-order mode control concept. The long slot can switch between broadside and dual-beam patterns by exciting different slot modes (full-wavelength slot or second-order slot mode). To validate the high-order mode control concept, a pattern reconfigurable slot antenna is designed, fabricated, and measured. By switching different feeding paths, the reconfigurable antenna can obtain a pair of complementary beams. Besides, the measured peak gains for these two modes are 11.1 dBi and 7.0 dBi, respectively. The proposed reconfigurable antenna boasts a simple yet ingenious structure (low cost), high gain, broadband capabilities, and excellent pattern diversity. It is an ideal candidate for intelligent wireless applications, including IoT, WiFi, FTTR, and microcells.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna by Using Multiple Feeds
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, an ultrawideband horizontally polarized omnidirectional antenna (HPOA) covering 1.47 GHz to 6.07 GHz (122%) is designed to behave stable main beam directions in vertical plane. In order to stabilize its radiation patterns, three measures are made through reassigning electric field distribution in slotline structures by using multiple feeds: decrease the spacing of each pair of monopolar modes, decrease the number of monopolar modes, and eliminate the anti-phase current loop. As seen from measured results, the designed HPOA has gain variations of less than 2 dB in horizontal plane and variations of main beam directions of less than 4° in vertical plane within working band. Therefore, the designed antenna is promising for LTE/5G/WiFi indoor communication systems especially in data-intensive regions.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Avian Rib-Inspired Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A broadband biomimetic antenna inspired by avian rib structures is presented in this letter. The antenna is composed of an arched dipole and two pairs of asymmetrical L-shaped stubs, along with dielectric materials conformally embedded to match the contour of avian ribs. Characteristic mode analysis is employed to analyze the operation of the antenna, revealing that the bandwidth expansion is attributed to the excitation of three modes. A prototype of the antenna is then fabricated and measured. The experiments are in good agreement with the simulation, and the results demonstrate that the antenna has a bandwidth of 50.8% with a 10 dB impedance bandwidth, exhibiting omnidirectional radiation and relatively stable gain. This antenna is suitable for use in frequencies used for Global System for Mobile Communication; Industrial, Scientific, and Medical applications; aerospace navigation systems; and the up-link control links of autonomous aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Switchable Metasurface With Radiation and Scattering Functions
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband switchable integrated metasurface with in-band scattering and radiation capabilities based on the Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase. The proposed integrated metasurface is composed of units with different rotations, and its radiation and scattering properties are endowed by loading a bias network. In order to effectively and independently control the radiation and scattering properties of the metasurface, it is possible to achieve this by controlling the states of the p-i-n diodes in the bias network. When the p-i-n diodes are in the <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</small>-state, the designed metasurface has scattering properties. For normal incidence, it achieves a radar cross section (RCS) reduction of 10 dB in the frequency range of 5.5-9.6 GHz. On the contrary, in the <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on-</small>state, the metasurface is converted into a circularly polarized (CP) antenna with radiation function, which has an axial ratio (AR) of 3 dB in the frequency bandwidth of 6.05 to 9.77 GHz. To verify the radiation and scattering characteristics of the designed metasurface, a 4×4 units metasurface structure is fabricated. The measurement results are in good agreement with the simulation results, and the RCS reduction band completely covers the working band of the antenna.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning-Based Optimization Method for Polarization-Rotation Element in Broadband and High-Aperture-Efficiency Metalens Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A machine-learning-based method is utilized to design and optimize the polarization rotation element (PRE) used for the design of broadband and high-aperture-efficiency metalens antenna (MLA) in this letter. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are employed to establish a library mapping the geometrical parameters of the PRE to the primary electromagnetic responses. Subsequently, genetic algorithm (GA) is applied to the predicted library to comprehensively optimize the geometrical parameters, achieving the target responses. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, an MLA prototype, which consists of 43 × 43 PREs is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results closely align with the simulations. The experimental result shows that the peak aperture efficiency could reach 63.79% at 10 GHz, and the corresponding gain is 27.73 dBi. More importantly, the bandwidths of 1 dB and 3 dB gain are measured to be 37.34% and 57.48%, respectively.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional Long Short-Term Memory-Based Amplitude and Phase Prediction of Antenna Array
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network to predict the excitations of antenna arrays for arbitrary radiation patterns. Compared to artificial neural networks (ANN) and unidirectional long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, BiLSTM effectively captures phase, amplitude, and inter-element dependencies by processing sequences in forward and backward directions. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that BiLSTM surpasses ANN and LSTM in accuracy. These findings highlight BiLSTM's potential to significantly improve electromagnetic field analysis and advance practical applications in antenna design and measurement.

articleTitle: W-band Ultra-Thin Hybrid Huygens Metasurface Transmit-Reflectarray with Independent Regulation of Transmit-Reflected Wave
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel high-efficiency ultra-thin hybrid Huygens metasurface (HMS) with independent regulation of transmit-reflected wave is proposed. Dual pairs of U-shaped and cross-shaped patches are used to form the multi-resonance hybrid HMS elements and realize efficient transmission and reflection simultaneously. Owing to the polarization orthogonality, Y-polarization transmission and X-polarization reflection waves can be regulated independently. Therefore, dual-functional array of efficient transmission and reflection can be achieved based on the hybrid HMS. Subsequently, a hybrid HMS-based transmit-reflectarray (TRA) prototype is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured peak aperture efficiencies are 46.33%/40.09% at 85 GHz with big bandwidth over 16%/28% for RA/TA. Different from conventional multi-layer arrays, the proposed TRA is implemented solely on single-layer substrate, thus the dielectric loss is minimized and design is greatly simplified. Benefiting from advantages of high-efficiency, single-layer as well as independent regulation capability of transmit-reflected waves, the proposed hybrid HMS-based TRA is expected to be a competitive candidate for communication systems in high frequency band of millimeter wave (MMW).

articleTitle: Dual-Band Single-Patch MIMO Antenna with Capacitor-Loaded Shorting Posts (CLSPs) as Modal Tuners
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces a novel dual-band decoupling concept using capacitor-loaded shorting posts (CLSPs) as modal tuners to align the resonances of TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> with TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, respectively. Leveraging modal superposition of two pairs of anti-phase current modes, a dual-band, dual-port single-patch antenna is developed, operating in the 3.5 GHz and 5.5 GHz frequency bands. Measurements confirm the design's effectiveness, improving the isolation from 3.5 dBi to over 12 dB, with peak gains of 6.5 dBi and 7.1 dBi in the respective bands.

articleTitle: A Compact Wide-Beam Open-Loop Antenna for Small Flight Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a compact wide-beam open-loop antenna is presented for small flight vehicle communication applications. The object is comprised of a disc-shaped metal pedestal and a vertical substrate. The primary radiated structure is the open loop, which is printed on the vertical substrate and fed by an edge coaxial line. Wide beam characteristics have been verified at 3.542 GHz to 3.612 GHz, with a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of 278° and 240° in the xoz- and yoz-planes, respectively. The total dimensions are calculated as π × 0.2λ0 × 0.2λ0 × 0.09λ0, where λ0 represents the wavelength of the central frequency in free space. The suggested design prototype has been fabricated and evaluated inside the microwave anechoic chamber, and the measured results closely correspond to the simulated. With its wide beam, compact size, lightweight, and affordable price, the suggested design is anticipated to be a good candidate for small flight vehicle applications.

articleTitle: A Uniplanar, Quasi-Isotropic Folded Dipole Design Based on Hybrid GA-PSO Optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A uniplanar quasi-isotropic folded dipole is proposed by using a hybrid genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization (GA-PSO) algorithm. The proposed antenna is evolved from a half-wave dipole, where the dipole is folded to achieve a pair of out-of-phase line sources and an orthogonal line source, thereby obtaining a quasi-isotropic radiation pattern. Based on GA-PSO algorithm, the bending position is optimized for the minimum gain difference. For demonstration, the dipole prototype operating at 915 MHz is designed and fabricated in which a parallel transmission line with comb-like structure is adopted to achieve good impedance matching. The measured result shows a gain difference of 2.81 dB, and the simulated value is 0.34 dB. Compared with other quasi-isotropic antennas, the proposed antenna has merits of simple structure, low gain difference and uniplanar structure.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Artificial Magnetic Conductor Integrated Low Frequency Quad Band Microstrip Antenna for Underground Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The challenges adhere to design planar antenna for versatile soil condition in wireless underground communication has grabbed the attention of potential researchers and is the present state-of-the-art research. Specifically, the change in underground soil properties (with time and place) demands the requirement of planar antennas (≤1000MHz) with varied operating frequencies. However, designing such antenna with good radiation profile is undeniably thought-provoking as they suffer from very poor gain (usually negative). In this communication, a completely new concept of heterogeneous AMC with quasi-AMC properties has been exploited to yield 4 frequency bands (≤1000MHz) with good measured gains of 3 dBi, 4.1 dBi, 7.8 dBi, 7.5 dBi at 703 MHz, 835 MHz, 937 MHz and 1008 MHz respectively. Despite having a smaller ground plane (0.4λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.4λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), the proposed antenna exhibits good gain and efficiencies in the range of 66% - 92%. The present investigation aims to design the simple and efficient antenna structure which is judiciously achieved through the thoughtful modulation of AMC ground plane impedance.

articleTitle: Simplified Theoretical Characterization on Polarized Beam Using Axially Quad-Sectored Impedance Modulated Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a simplified and novel theoretical characterization of orthogonal and out of phase incorporated, axially quad-sectored impedance modulated metasurface antennas (IMMAs). Surface impedances (Zsurf) of proposed orthogonal and out of phase modulated metasurface antenna (MA) is numerically modeled and discussed with necessary simulated and measured data. Orthogonal phase modulated metasurface possess a circularly polarized (CP) single beam towards (${\theta _0}$,${\varphi _0}$) = (0$^\circ $,0$^\circ $) with a peak gain (gmax) = 22.11dBic. On the other hand, out of phase modulated MA possess a linearly polarized (LP) single beam towards (${\theta _0}$,${\varphi _0}$) = (0$^\circ $,0$^\circ $) with a peak gain (gmax) = 22.11dBi. Both MAs consist an overall dimension of 10.5 ${\lambda _0} \times $ 10.5${\lambda _0}$ at f0 = 25GHz. Wide axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) with AR<0.9dB and >32dB cross-pol isolation is obtained for proposed CP and LP MAs respectively. The beauty of phase modulation and its performance characterization to obtain polarization alteration between linear and circularly polarized (LP and CP) impedance modulated surface (IMS)s is the prime observation from this letter.

articleTitle: Compact and Gain-Enhanced Vivaldi Antenna Design Using Nonuniform Slot Profile Optimization and Aperture Dielectric Loading
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces an efficient and compact design for ultra- wideband (UWB) applications, achieving both size reduction and enhanced gain. By using nonuniform slot lines as the radiation structure and adding extended ground branches, the design achieves significant miniaturization. The antenna circuit length is reduced from 27.2 mm to 14 mm, and the substrate from 41 mm × 48 mm to 32 mm × 25 mm, while maintaining a gain of 3.2 to 7.4 dBi. Additionally, a Synergistic Coupling Board and a compact dielectric lens structure are loaded, which increases the gain to 4.1 to 9.6 dBi and significantly enhances the radiation directivity. The experimental and simulation results show good consistency. This study realizes the miniaturization and maintains the gain, which verifies the effectiveness of the miniaturization design.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-band Filter-Antenna Based on Characteristic Mode Theory Using Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this paper, a Ka-band filter-antenna based on Gap Waveguide (GWG) is proposed. Firstly, a patch of the filter-antenna with a flat in-band gain and good out-of-band rejection, is analyzed using Characteristic Mode Theory (CMT). Secondly, dispersion diagram of a novel mushroom unit cell with four metallized vias is presented. Thirdly, a resonator based on a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) with high quality, along with a GWG feeding line, is added to excite the desired modes. Finally, for integration and measurement considerations, transition structures are designed from the GWG to the microstrip line (MSL) and from the MSL to the coupling slot, and the proposed filter-antenna worked at ka-band is obtained. The measurement results show that the impedance bandwidth of the proposed filter-antenna ranges from 34.3 GHz to 36.9 GHz and the in-band gain is about 8.5 dBi, while the out-of-band rejection levels at the low and high frequency nulls are about 45 dB and 32 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: On the Filtering Dielectric Resonator Transmitarray
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter reports the first filtering dielectric resonator (DR) transmitarray that directs an incident wave to a designed direction. The DR elements are three-dimensional devices made of a dielectric material. The unit cell of the filtering transmitarray has symmetric lower and upper DR grids for receiving and transmitting energy, each having a cross-slot on the metal plate to couple energy to each other. Each DR grid has 4×4 small rectangular DRs, supported by a hollow substrate. To flexibly design the radiation-beam direction, a full phase range of 0°-360° is obtained by varying the DR size and thus its resonant frequency. At the lower filtering edge, At the lower filtering edge, the opposing electric fields is caused by the odd-mode coupling between the lower and upper cross-slots, giving one lower-edge transmission zero. For the upper filtering edge, the field cancellation is due to the DR grid resonating at a harmonic mode, providing the upper-edge transmission zero. The transmission passband is obtained by the coupling of a quasi-TE111 mode of each DR grid and a resonant cross-slot mode. For demonstration, a 26-GHz DR filtering transmitarray prototype consisting of 16×16 DR grids was designed, fabricated, and tested. It has a peak realized antenna gain of 19.07 dBi, structure profile of 0.33λ0, and 3-dB gain bandwidth of 15.4% (23.9 - 27.9 GHz). The bandwidth can cover the 5G mm-wave frequency band (24.75-27.5 GHz)

articleTitle: Ultra-Short Horn Antennas via Digital Choke and Groove Aperture Topologies
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The pursuit of compact antennas has historically sacrificed directivity. Traditionally, solutions involve adding radiators, complex lenses, or enlarging the antenna, which often introduces spurious lobes or increases system height. This study investigates a digital choke and groove aperture technology, employing recessed slots and protruded chokes, to optimize directivity and shape lobes in ultra-short horns. Through analysis and experiments, we assess the antenna's gain, volume efficiency, bandwidth, and lobe suppression. Our findings offer insights into applications and lay the groundwork for further advancements in ultra-low-profile digital aperture topologies for ultra-short horns.
